THE FIVE PROOFS THE RULING REQUIRES, EACH AS A REFUSAL, because an authorization suite that mostly shows permitted callers being permitted proves the happy path and nothing about the boundary. (1) A protected route refuses with no account -- and a PROFILE route refuses on the account floor BEFORE the profile is examined, asserted by requiring the internal detail not to mention profile access, because evaluating the profile first would make "no such profile" observable to somebody who is not logged in. (2) The decision function takes NO profile id at all, asserted structurally against the source: there is no parameter a caller-supplied id could arrive through, which is the route-level form of the forgeable-ProfileScope bypass PL-0405 recorded. (3) THE LAUNCH TOKEN IS NOT A LOGIN, proven by the type signature rather than by a test that passes a header and checks it was ignored -- authorizeRoute is never given a Request, so it cannot consult the token even by accident, and the source is asserted to contain no bare `Request` type, no `headers`, and no `sidecar`. The behavioural half is there too: a caller that satisfied PW-0101's listener guard completely and carries no account is refused as unauthenticated. (4) All three not_permitted causes -- not owned, no ownership record, no active profile -- are BYTE-IDENTICAL on the wire, asserted as a one-element Set over wireDetail and over code, while STAYING DISTINCT in the internal detail, because hiding the difference from the operator too would make an authorization failure indistinguishable from a routing bug. 404 is refused for a profile the caller may not see, for the same reason. (5) LOOPBACK IS NEVER AUTHENTICATION: the source may not contain 127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost, x-forwarded-for or remoteAddress, with a non-vacuity assertion so the comment stripper is not eating the file. SECOND FILE, handler-authorization.test.ts, guards what the audit found ALREADY CORRECT across all three profile-scoped handlers: each resolves a request context; none reads a profile id by any of four spellings; the two data handlers authorize the ACTIVE profile via resolveActiveProfileScope; the external reason vocabulary cannot name a missing profile, asserted against the union declaration in packages/auth; and no handler mentions an address or the launch token. The profiles picker is exempt AND NAMED -- selection necessarily runs before any profile is active, which is why @liberty/auth publishes a separate selection decision. It opens with a non-vacuity check that every guarded file was actually read. TWO HARNESS DEFECTS FOUND AND REPORTED RATHER THAN WIDENED AWAY: an assertion forbidding the word Request matched RequestAccountResolution and was narrowed by removing the known identifiers first, not by dropping the check; and an assertion bounding the external reason union by a 300-character window reached into the narrowing switch below it, where profile_not_found legitimately appears as a case -- that is the mapping working, not the leak -- and is now bounded to the declaration itself.

WHAT THE 49 TESTS ARE FOR, BY THE PROPERTY THEY DEFEND. NO CLIENT-HELD SCOPE, WHICH IS THE SECURITY CORE: listProfiles is asserted to send no body, no query and no id, and the URL is asserted not to contain a question mark -- PL-0405 recorded a forgeable-scope defect and a ?profileId= on a read is exactly how it comes back. selectProfile is asserted to be the only function that sends an id, to send it in the body of the selection route and never in the path or a query, and to pass a malformed id straight through rather than pre-judging it, because isMintedProfileId is the single authority and a second pattern here would answer request_malformed where the first answers profile_unavailable -- itself a small oracle. message: PW-0302 NOT CLAIMED THIS ROUND, and the audit is why. Its acceptance says artwork must be a contract change carrying 'dimensions and a rights basis beside the URL rather than a bare string'. The repository already has an artwork vocabulary and it deliberately has NO URL in it: artworkRefSchema in packages/catalog-ingestion/src/record.ts carries role (poster|backdrop|still), an assetRef constrained to an opaque lower-case token, and a REQUIRED rights basis -- required there and nowhere else in that package, on the stated argument that a work with an undeclared basis is merely refused from browse while an image with an undeclared basis that reached a page would be somebody else's file served from our origin. Its comment says in capitals that assetRef IS AN OPAQUE INTERNAL IDENTIFIER AND NEVER A URL, because a provider's image CDN link is a media address in a catalog payload. project.ts then DROPS artwork on the way to CatalogItem, and packages/contracts/src/domains/catalog.ts opens by saying the browse shape carries no stream, URL or provider field. So PW-0302 as written would put a URL into the one contract whose header promises there is none, and would create a second artwork vocabulary beside a deliberate one. THE RECONCILIATION I BELIEVE IS RIGHT, offered for ruling rather than implemented: the contract adopts artworkRefSchema's shape -- role, opaque assetRef, dimensions, required rights -- and still carries no URL; the URL is produced at the rendering boundary by a resolver that maps an assetRef onto an origin from the allowlist. Then next/image remotePatterns pinned to the allowlist is not a check that could be forgotten but a structural fact, because no other origin is expressible, and SECURITY.md's never proxy arbitrary client-provided URLs holds without a guard. That satisfies the acceptance's INTENT -- not a bare string, dimensions and rights beside it, allowlisted origins -- while contradicting its literal words about a URL in the contract. PW-0403 allowedPaths widened before implementation, derived from the acceptance rather than from convenience, and each entry has a reason the acceptance cannot be met without. (1) apps/web/src/lib/db/index.ts -- the auth instance needs a PostgreSQL handle, and this module already builds exactly one per connection string per process while DISCARDING the handle that createPostgresRepository returns beside the repository. The alternative inside the original surface was a second pg pool opened from the session lane, which would break that module's own stated invariant of at most one pool per connection string. Exposing the handle is the smaller change and the correct architecture. (2) apps/web/src/lib/db/request-context.ts, the three route groups' contract.ts files, and docs/API_CONTRACTS.md -- because a deployment that CAN authenticate must be able to say a request is NOT authenticated, and no such reason code exists. RequestAccountRefusalReason has exactly two members, authentication_not_configured and development_identifier_malformed, and neither is true of a request that simply presented no valid session; answering authentication_not_configured there would tell an operator to wire an auth instance that is already wired. The union is published: accountRefusalCode widens it into RequestContextReasonCode by identity and each route group enumerates every code it can answer, so adding a member is an API-contract change across those files by construction, and product invariant 5 requires the contract to change intentionally first. Their earlier presence in reviewDependencies is removed where they are now writable, since ai:validate correctly reports a reviewDependency inside an allowedPath as redundant. EXECUTED on da94ef4. cd apps/web && npx vitest run over the three suites -> account 19, deployment-session 21, auth-instance 12, exit 0; monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 packages, exit 0, apps/web at 1109 tests, up from 1075, every other package unchanged. NO POSTGRESQL AND NO AUTH LIBRARY IS NEEDED BY ANY OF THEM, which is a design property rather than a convenience: deploymentSessionAccount takes the session reader as an argument and selectAuthInstance takes every input explicitly, the same shape selectRepository already uses, so no suite mutates process.env and none races another in the same worker. WHAT THE 52 TESTS DEFEND. THE FOUR SESSION FAILURES ARE ONE ANSWER: absent, absent-spelled-undefined, malformed, expired and revoked are each a named case, each asserted to produce not_authenticated with one identical detail, and a further test collects the details into a Set and requires its size to be exactly 1 -- so the wordings cannot drift apart into four answers that can be told apart. That is the non-oracle discipline PW-0402's review required preserved, applied on the authentication side. WHAT CANNOT SUBSTITUTE FOR A SESSION is asserted as three ABSENCES, which is the only form that stays true when somebody later adds a header read for the desktop case: a request carrying both an Authorization bearer and an x-liberty-desktop-token is refused, a request from 127.0.0.1 with matching origin, host and x-forwarded-for is refused, and a request carrying both development headers is refused. A fourth test states it positively: the reader is handed request.headers BY IDENTITY and the function has no other channel into the request, so a later edit that passed the URL or the body fails. A SESSION THAT IS PRESENT BUT UNUSABLE IS NOT AN IDENTITY: six cases -- no user, no session, empty user id, empty session id, non-string id, null user -- all fail CLOSED as not_authenticated rather than as a server error. The empty-string cases are the reason the check exists: an empty id compares EQUAL to another empty id, so a defect upstream would silently merge households rather than fail. NEITHER ID REACHES THE TRAIL, asserted directly, because a session id in a log aggregator is a credential-shaped value and an account id is the one profileViewSchema already refuses to publish. THE STORE FAILING IS NOT THE VIEWER BEING SIGNED OUT: a thrown read reports authentication_not_configured, not not_authenticated, because retry-later is true of one and false of the other, and a thrown non-Error is asserted not to put the word undefined on the screen. THE COMPOSITION ROOT IS TESTED ONLY ON ITS REFUSALS, and that is deliberate -- constructing the instance needs a real Drizzle handle over a real pool, and a stub of one is a stub of Better Auth's constructor, which is the argument better-auth.ts itself makes for having no unit tests. The refusals are the part that decides whether a misconfigured deployment fails safe: the store is checked BEFORE configuration so an operator with no DATABASE_URL is not sent to fix a secret first; the in-memory adapter is refused outright; a PostgreSQL store with no connection string supplied is refused as two different reads of the environment; a short secret is refused, which is the dangerous class because a 12-character secret produces a WORKING system with forgeable cookies; a wildcard trusted origin is refused because the schema requires a URL; every problem is reported at once; and a refusal is asserted to contain neither the secret nor the password from the connection string. TWO SOURCE-LEVEL RULES: every process.env read is inside a function body, so the answer is not frozen to whatever the process looked like when the first route loaded, and the module contains exactly ONE throw -- the mail transport's, which is a rejected promise at send time -- with the count asserted rather than the keyword forbidden, because a ban would be relaxed the first time somebody adds a legitimate one and would then mean nothing. The mail placeholder is asserted to contain no console. and no message.url, because the two wrong defaults createLibertyAuth names are dropping the mail silently and logging a one-click account-takeover link.

THE TOKEN IS ASSERTED NOT TO APPEAR IN ANY ARGUMENT: launch_arguments is built from a planned launch whose token is a real 64-character value, and every argument is asserted not to contain it while the environment IS asserted to carry it. That is the PW-0101 property from the other side -- a Windows process's command line is readable by any process running as the same user and is shown in Task Manager, so argv would publish the one value separating our listener from every other local process. NO FAILURE REPORT MAY CONTAIN THE TOKEN: all six startup failures are described and scanned, and the Token arm is deliberately CONSTRUCTED with the token embedded in its inner message so that forwarding that message would fail the test -- the arm drops it and says so. A NON-LOOPBACK HANDSHAKE HOST IS REFUSED: 0.0.0.0, a LAN address, a domain and localhost are each refused, and this is a RESTATEMENT of a rule apps/web/src/lib/sidecar/handshake.ts already enforces, not an inheritance of it. The justification is in the module: this process is the one that acts on the value by pointing a webview at it, and a compromised or simply buggy child is exactly the case where the producer's check did not run, so a consumer that trusted the producer would be trusting the thing it validates. AN UNUSABLE PORT IS REFUSED RATHER THAN WRAPPED: 0, -1, 70000, 65536, a string and null. 70000 narrowed to u16 is 4464, a perfectly plausible port, which is why the range check precedes the narrowing. IPv6 IS BRACKETED: http://::1:41999/ is not a URL and the shell would silently fail to navigate. ORDINARY LOG LINES ARE NOT ERRORS while a handshake-shaped line with no body IS -- the caller reads every line the child prints, so collapsing those two would either report a broken contract on Next's startup banner or swallow a genuinely broken one. THE RESTART BUDGET: four consecutive failures then a stated failure, never an unbounded loop behind a blank window; a healthy run clears the budget BEFORE its own failure is charged, so a crash after an hour is a first failure rather than a fifth; the boundary at MIN_HEALTHY_RUN minus one millisecond is asserted, because roughly twenty seconds is not a rule; the backoff shift is asserted not to overflow at u32::MAX, because 1 << attempt is undefined past 63 and the input is a counter; and the worst-case total wait before the user is told something is asserted under fifteen seconds, because that total is what a person actually experiences. THE LAUNCH PLAN: a short or non-hex token is refused before anything is spawned, since this process MINTS it and learning at the sidecar's bind check that the shell generated rubbish would put the failure in the wrong half of the system; a missing runtime names what is missing and where, because an incomplete-installation message with no path is a support ticket nobody can act on; and resources are asserted to resolve under the directory given rather than the current one, which is the difference between working under cargo run and failing in an installed build. FIVE TESTS ARE WINDOWS-BEHAVIOUR-SHAPED AND ARE NOT CLAIMED AS SUCH: job.rs's tests assert the error text names which step failed, and that a non-Windows build REFUSES rather than silently running unsupervised. Whether the kernel terminates job members is not asserted by anything here and cannot be from this environment.

Monorepo unchanged: npm run typecheck 21/21, npm run lint 11/11 zero problems, npm run repo:validate passed. The new workflow parses as YAML with one job, windows-shell, on windows-latest, seven steps. ONE PACKAGING FACT FOUND AND FIXED: apps/desktop/dist/index.html was silently ignored by the ROOT .gitignore's dist/ rule. Everywhere else in this repository dist/ is build output; here it is a single hand-written failure page named by tauri.conf.json as frontendDist, with no build step that could regenerate it, so an ignored copy means a packaged shell with no page to show when it has something to say. EXECUTED on a3d70f5. cargo test --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -> 42 passed, 0 failed, exit 0, up from 25. Monorepo suite unchanged at 20/20 with apps/web at 1109; this task adds no TypeScript. THE SEVENTEEN NEW TESTS ARE ABOUT THE ASSEMBLY, which is what the round-87 verdict said was missing, and they are possible because the assembly is a SEQUENCE behind a trait rather than a function full of syscalls. THE CENTRAL ORDERING ASSERTION: create_job before spawn, spawn before assign, assign before the handshake, handshake before show_window -- each checked by position in a recorded call list. A job created after the spawn has nothing to assign; a window shown before a handshake is a window pointed at a port nothing is listening on. THE TOKEN, at the point where a process is actually created: absent from every spawn argument, present in the environment under LIBERTY_SIDECAR_TOKEN. sidecar.rs already asserts this of launch_arguments; this re-asserts it where somebody would one day add an argument. A TOKEN THAT CANNOT BE MINTED STOPS THE LAUNCH: nothing is spawned and a failure is surfaced, because every fallback source is predictable to the local processes the token excludes. A JOB THAT CANNOT BE CREATED REFUSES TO START rather than running unsupervised, and the surfaced text is asserted to explain that choice -- a user not told why nothing opened will think it crashed. A CHILD THAT CANNOT BE ASSIGNED IS KILLED, asserted by position: the kill follows the failed assign and no window is shown. An unassigned running child is the orphan itself. THE ORIGIN COMES FROM WHAT THE CHILD REPORTED: an IPv6 handshake produces http://[::1]:50000, bracketed, because the unbracketed form is not a URL and the shell would silently fail to navigate. A REJECTED HANDSHAKE IS NOT RETRIED -- exactly one spawn -- because a broken contract will not fix itself on the fourth attempt and retrying delays the message that says what happened. A TIMEOUT IS RETRIED WITHIN THE BUDGET AND THEN SURFACED, bounded between two and six spawns. A HEALTHY RUN THAT ENDS IS RESTARTED AND A FLAPPING ONE IS NOT, which exercises the supervision policy THROUGH the assembly rather than only in isolation, so the loop must actually consult it. A MISSING INSTALLATION IS NOT RETRIED and never reaches a job. AND NO FAILURE PATH PANICS: eight distinct failures are each run and each asserted to surface something, because a shell that panics is a window that closes itself. THE TOKEN MODULE ADDS FIVE: the minted token satisfies TOKEN_MIN_CHARS as lower-case hex asserted against the constant rather than the literal; 64 mints produce 64 distinct tokens, because per-launch is the whole property; 256 tokens are checked for prefix distinctness and hex-digit distribution, which is not a statistical test and is not claimed as one -- it catches a source that is a counter, a timestamp or a padded constant; hex encoding is checked directly; and a source scan asserts the module reaches for no SystemTime, Instant, process::id, rand:: or hostname. THAT LAST TEST FAILED ON ITS FIRST RUN by matching its own forbidden-word list, which is a guard matching prose about the thing rather than the thing -- the fifth instance in this repository and written minutes after PL-AI-0013 was approved for that class. It is scoped to the code above the test module and the comment records the miss. ONE HARNESS DEFECT WORTH RECORDING: the fake's first draft repeated its last run duration forever, and with a healthy duration that is an infinite loop -- the suite was SIGKILLed. RE-RECORDED on a3d70f5. STILL FAIL, and now for exactly one reason: THE WINDOWS JOB HAS NOT RUN, BECAUSE THE BRANCH CANNOT BE PUSHED. It was produced by me running 'ai-control-plane.mjs event --help' to read the subcommand's usage: 'event' takes its first positional argument as the event TYPE and has no help flag, so the probe recorded itself. The line is left in place deliberately. Removing it would be editing the audit trail to hide an operator mistake, which is the practice gpt-architect ruled against in round 85 for the round-83 incident history, and the same rule applies to a harmless mistake as to a consequential one -- a log that is edited when the mistake is small is not evidence when the mistake is large. Anything reading this log should treat the '--help' event as a no-op with no taskId, no agent and no claim attached.

PW-0302 allowedPaths widened by ten entries, recorded BEFORE any file is written, following the procedure gpt-architect required for PW-0102 in round 88. EVERY ENTRY IS DERIVED FROM THE RECONCILED ACCEPTANCE, and the audit that produced it is stated here so the reviewer can check the derivation rather than the outcome.

WHY THE DECLARED SURFACE COULD NOT MEET THE ACCEPTANCE. The four declared paths were domains/catalog.ts, domains/title.ts, components/artwork/** and next.config.ts. That surface can declare an artwork vocabulary and configure an image loader. It cannot contain (a) the vocabulary itself, because contracts keeps leaf vocabularies -- rights, ids, codecs, drm, media-facts, runtime -- in src/shared and a domain module that declared one would be the second rights.ts; (b) the resolution boundary, which the acceptance requires and which is a route handler; (c) the rendering site, because the only poster in the browse surface is a div in catalog-card.tsx; (d) the adoption requirement, because artworkRefSchema lives in catalog-ingestion/src/record.ts and 'adopts rather than invents a second one' is only structurally true if one definition exists; (e) any artwork data at all, so the path would be typed and never exercised.

THE TEN ENTRIES AND THE CLAUSE EACH ANSWERS.
packages/contracts/src/shared/artwork.ts -- 'the catalog and title contracts carry an OPAQUE ARTWORK REFERENCE plus required display metadata and a rights basis'. A leaf module beside rights.ts, for the reason rights.ts states about itself: every domain that needs the vocabulary reaches it directly, so there is no path by which a second one comes into existence.
packages/contracts/src/artwork.test.ts, catalog.test.ts, title.test.ts -- the unit gate over the vocabulary and over the two domain shapes that gain the field.
packages/catalog-ingestion/src/record.ts -- 'The vocabulary ADOPTS artworkRefSchema's shape rather than inventing a second one; where the two must differ, say why in the module.' record.ts will import the role enum and the opaque assetRef primitive from the new leaf instead of spelling them again. Its composition is NOT changed: artworkRefSchema keeps ingestedRightsBasisSchema, because the ingestion record carries the operator's rights-register reference and a browse payload must not. That is the difference the acceptance asks to have explained, and it will be explained in both modules. Moved out of reviewDependencies, where 'packages/catalog-ingestion/src' still covers the rest of the package.
apps/web/src/app/api/v1/artwork/** -- 'an authorized artwork-resolution boundary turns the opaque reference into a fetchable or served asset'. A route handler and its policy, following the handler.ts/route.ts/contract.ts split the catalog and profiles routes already use.
apps/web/src/components/catalog-card.tsx -- 'user-facing artwork UI', and the only place the browse surface renders a poster. Its poster is a decorative aria-hidden gradient div; the artwork component replaces that element and keeps both properties.
apps/web/src/lib/demo-catalog.ts and apps/web/fixtures/artwork/** -- 'Titles have artwork'. With no licensed provider (PL-0302 and PL-0602 are BLOCKED on exactly that), the only way this path is exercised end to end rather than merely typed is the development fixtures, which are original works authored in this repository under an owned basis with a null register reference. The fixture images will be generated by a committed script and a README will state precisely what they are; they are a way to exercise the boundary, and nothing will present them as delivered product artwork.
docs/API_CONTRACTS.md -- invariant 5, which requires an API contract change to be recorded before it ships. Two published shapes gain a field and a new endpoint appears.

CONFLICT CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, PER ENTRY. apps/web/fixtures/artwork/** is named by no other task. Every other entry is covered only by tasks in a terminal state -- PL-0101, PL-0102, PL-0104, PL-0202, PL-0203, PL-0303, PL-0305, PL-0309, PL-0312, PL-0502, PL-0702, PL-0706, PL-0707, PL-0711, PL-0902, PL-AI-0002, PL-AI-0006 and PW-0403, all DONE -- or by PL-0302 and PL-0602, both BLOCKED on licensed provider and live-feed access and neither claimable today. The only other active task is PW-0102, whose surface is apps/desktop/** and .github/workflows/desktop-shell-ci.yml; it does not intersect any entry here.

It is NOT needed: the repository already has a CSS-module precedent for exactly this situation -- search.module.css and title.module.css both say in their headers that they are modules because globals.css was outside their task's paths -- so the artwork component carries its own module and composes with the existing global .poster class rather than editing it. The hero has no poster slot, so rendering there is a .hero layout change in globals.css -- the file just declined -- plus title.module.css and its style test. message:
PW-0305 IS DEFERRED BEHIND PW-0302'S REVIEW, AND PW-0401 IS TAKEN INSTEAD. The commander's round-89 wave order is PW-0302, then PW-0305, then PW-0401. PW-0305 is skipped this wave for a stated reason rather than a convenient one.

THE FINDING. PW-0305's acceptance has four REQUIRED clauses. Three of them -- the continue-watching rail on home, resume through the session's startAtSeconds, and a start-over control -- are reachable from its declared surface plus apps/web/src/app/page.tsx. The fourth is not: 'a progress indicator on cards for partially watched titles' names the CARDS, and the only card in the browse surface is apps/web/src/components/catalog-card.tsx, which PW-0302 holds in allowedPaths and which is in REVIEW awaiting gpt-architect. A partially watched title appearing in the Films rail has to show progress there too, or the indicator is a property of one rail rather than of a title.

WHAT I DID NOT DO ABOUT IT. I did not build a second card component under components/continue-watching/** carrying its own progress bar. That would satisfy conflictWithActive by standing a duplicate of catalog-card.tsx beside it -- two hand-maintained renderings of the same thing, free to drift, which is the defect demo-catalog.ts records as the reason it derives its rails from one declaration. I also did not widen PW-0305 into a file an active task holds, and I did not release PW-0302 from REVIEW to free the file: gate results are discarded on release, so that would destroy this round's recorded evidence to save a sequencing wait.

WHY PW-0401 INSTEAD. It is READY, dispatchable, conflict-free -- its surface is apps/backend/**, which no other task names and which does not exist yet -- and it is the commander's own next item. The round-85 instruction is explicit that pending reviews are not a reason to idle: keep other conflict-free lanes moving. PW-0305 becomes dispatchable the moment PW-0302 leaves REVIEW in either direction, approved or changes-requested, because either outcome frees catalog-card.tsx or returns it to an owner who can sequence the two.

NO TASK DEFINITION WAS CHANGED BY THIS FINDING. PW-0305 is untouched and still READY with its declared surface intact; this event records the order and the reason, nothing else.

PW-0401 allowedPaths gain two entries beyond apps/backend/**, recorded BEFORE any file is written, and the audit that forced them is stated here because it found TWO ARCHITECTURAL FORKS the reviewer should rule on rather than inherit.

THE ENTRIES.
package-lock.json -- apps/backend is a new workspace under the root's apps/* glob, and a workspace absent from the lockfile breaks npm ci in CI. Mechanical, unavoidable, and held only by tasks in a terminal state.
apps/web/package.json -- an exports map, for the reason in FORK 1 below. BOARD OVERLAP REPORTED RATHER THAN ACTED ON: PW-0104 (READY, unclaimed) also declares this file. It is not an active conflict today and conflictWithActive will refuse the pair the moment PW-0104 is claimed. The two changes touch different keys -- PW-0104 edits the dev and build scripts over next-env.d.ts, this adds an exports map -- so the overlap is real but not contradictory, and sequencing is the remedy rather than narrowing either one.

FORK 1 -- WHERE THE PLAYBACK-SESSION DECISION LIVES, AND WHY I DID NOT EXTRACT IT.
The acceptance requires 'the same route contract, byte for byte'. backend-stub.mjs already argues the general case in its own header: it deliberately relays rather than reimplements, because 'a stub that reimplemented the decision would be a second opinion about it'. That applies with more force to the real service: two implementations of invariants 1 and 2, free to drift, is the outcome this repository rejects everywhere else.
So there must be ONE implementation, and today it lives in apps/web/src/app/api/v1/playback/session -- contract.ts, authorized-candidates.ts, issue-session.ts, playback-session-implementation.ts and handler.ts. PW-0401 is the SECOND CALLER, which is normally exactly the event that turns 'this should be a package' into 'extract it now', and two contract.ts headers in this repository already record that placement as follow-up rather than as a decision.
I DID NOT EXTRACT IT, and the reason is a security guard rather than effort. apps/web/src/app/api/v1/playback/build-target.test.ts is what proves docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8's central property -- that a desktop bundle contains no provider-resolution implementation. Its walker follows RELATIVE specifiers only; a non-relative specifier is RECORDED as a package name and not walked into. Extracting the resolver behind @liberty/playback-resolution would therefore put @liberty/provider-sdk and @liberty/media-engine on the far side of a boundary that walker does not cross. The desktop assertion would still pass, for the wrong reason, and the suite's own non-vacuity assertion -- that the WEB graph DOES reach those two packages, which exists precisely so a walker that silently resolved nothing cannot look like an absence -- would fail or have to be weakened. Turning a real absence into an unobserved one, in the guard for the section-8 ruling, is not a cost I will pay for tidier layering inside a backend task.
WHAT I DID INSTEAD: apps/web/package.json gains a NARROW exports map exposing the playback-session modules and the session modules as subpaths, and apps/backend imports the decision and the authentication through it. One implementation, byte-for-byte by construction rather than by comparison, and the section-8 guard is untouched and exactly as strong as it is today.
WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: a service depending on the web application's package is a layering inversion. The correct long-term home for the decision is a package of its own. The honest PREREQUISITE for that extraction is teaching build-target.test.ts's walker to follow workspace packages -- which would make that guard STRONGER than it is today, since it currently cannot see inside any package boundary -- and that belongs to whoever owns the guard, not to a backend task reaching two directories up into the most heavily reviewed subsystem in the repository. If gpt-architect rules for the extraction, the service's own code does not change: only the three import specifiers at its top do.

FORK 2 -- HOW AN UNAUTHENTICATED CALLER IS REPORTED, WHICH I CANNOT FIX FROM HERE.
The acceptance requires caller authentication and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. The refusal is structurally non-leaking in this design, because authentication runs BEFORE the body is read at all, so the refusal cannot depend on a content id that has not been parsed -- and that is assertable by comparing the bytes of the refusal for a real id and an invented one.
THE PROBLEM IS WHAT THE DESKTOP THEN LEARNS. playbackSessionReasonCodeSchema is a CLOSED vocabulary with no authentication member, and the response status is derived from the OUTCOME alone -- granted, denied, unavailable -- so there is no shape in the published contract that means 401. A backend that answered 401 with an off-contract body is turned by the forwarder into unavailable / provider_unavailable, which is honest but lossy: the desktop cannot tell 'you are not signed in' from 'the backend is down'.
I DID NOT ADD A REASON CODE, because invariant 5 says the contract changes intentionally FIRST and that change would touch contract.ts, the status derivation, docs/API_CONTRACTS.md and the web route's published behaviour -- a surface far wider than apps/backend/** and one whose bodies the cross-target e2e suite compares byte for byte. It is also precisely the shape of change gpt-architect approved deliberately in PW-0403, where not_authenticated was added to the request-context vocabulary with the ruling 'do not collapse these states'. I am raising it as a proposed follow-up rather than making the same change unilaterally inside a task that does not own the contract.

NOTHING ELSE WAS TAKEN. The resolution modules, the section-8 guard, the contract, the docs and the e2e harness are all reviewDependencies, several of them added this round so the reviewer can see what these two decisions were measured against.

evidence: npm run typecheck at 8e8c3bf: turbo, 22 tasks, 22 successful, exit 0 -- one more than last round because @liberty/backend is a new workspace with its own tsc --noEmit over src/**/*.ts, esbuild.mjs and vitest.config.ts. npm run lint also passes (12 tasks, exit 0). THE TYPECHECK IS DOING REAL WORK ON THIS TASK RATHER THAN CONFIRMING SYNTAX: apps/backend consumes @liberty/web through a new exports map, and tsc resolving @liberty/web/playback-session/handler and @liberty/web/session/account to the declared .ts files under moduleResolution Bundler is what proves the subpaths are reachable as types and not only at bundle time. It is also what checks the two imported signatures this service is built on -- that handlePlaybackSessionRequest really is (Request) => Promise<Response> and that RequestAccountResolution's refusal union is exactly the three members the status table enumerates, so a fourth reason added upstream would fail the Record<RequestAccountRefusalReason, number> here rather than falling through to an undefined status. npm run build passes (12 tasks, exit 0) and includes the new esbuild bundle, dist/main.mjs at 3.2 MB with only pg external; the bundle contains zero occurrences of 'next/', which is the check that this service pulled the decision out of apps/web without pulling the framework with it.

npx turbo run test --force at 8e8c3bf: 22 tasks, 22 successful, exit 0, nothing cached. @liberty/backend contributes 3 files and 33 tests; every other workspace is unchanged in count, which is the regression evidence for the one edit outside apps/backend -- an exports map on apps/web/package.json. config.test.ts (11) covers the transport refusals, and the port test FOUND A REAL DEFECT rather than confirming the code: Number('1e3') is 1000 and Number('0x10') is 16, both integers in range, so the first implementation would have listened on a port the operator did not type; it now requires decimal digits and refuses everything else. session-endpoint.test.ts (16) is where the acceptance lives. It asserts the body is UNREAD at the moment of refusal (request.bodyUsed is false), that the refusal is byte-identical across six bodies -- a real id, an invented id, a malformed id, a body with no id, a non-JSON string and an empty string -- and that it echoes none of the ids it was asked about; that the upstream detail is not reflected, using a refusal whose detail quotes a script tag; that a decision throwing a message containing a postgres URL with a password produces the contract's unavailable shape with none of it; that the success path returns the decision's own Response object identically, which is 'byte for byte' as an identity check rather than a comparison; and three structural rules over source -- that the envelope is imported from @liberty/web/playback-session/handler, that no module in this service value-imports @liberty/media-engine or @liberty/provider-sdk (the beginning of a second opinion), and that no module names an api key, client secret, signing key or bearer literal. server.test.ts (6) binds an ephemeral port and drives the real bridge: body and method carried through, content-length matching the bytes sent, 404 and 405 routed, a 512 KiB body refused at 413 by the transport bound that sits deliberately looser than the contract's own MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES, and a hostile Host header not reaching the URL.

EXECUTED at 8e8c3bf, both modes, from e2e/, in the CI job's own configuration -- PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD unset so the pinned chromium 1234 resolves from Playwright's default cache, CI=1, CONTENT_RIGHTS_ENFORCEMENT=strict, LIBERTY_FC_SEED=20250819, LIBERTY_FIXTURE_MEDIA_ORIGIN=https://fixtures.invalid. Production: npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium -> 61 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. Development: LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development, same projects -> 70 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. Both counts are IDENTICAL to rounds 82 through 89, which is the whole content of this gate for this task: the only edit outside a new workspace is an exports map on apps/web/package.json, and adding an exports field to a package that previously had none is exactly the change that can silently break resolution for everything that imports it. It did not: the cross-target suite -- which starts a web-target server, a desktop-target server and the backend stub, and compares whole response bodies between the two targets -- passes unchanged in both modes.

WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT COVER, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE INFERRED. No Playwright spec exercises apps/backend. The harness still starts e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs as the forwarder's counterparty, and that is a deliberate outcome rather than work left undone: the desktop specs witness that the forwarder FORWARDED by reading the stub's /__requests ledger of every request it received, headers and body included, and a production backend must not have that ledger. Pointing the harness at this service is therefore not a configuration change -- it needs a different way to witness forwarding -- and e2e/** is outside this task's allowedPaths, so proposing that mechanism is a follow-up rather than something to smuggle in behind a gate.

WHAT REPLACES IT AS EVIDENCE, and it is stronger than a spec against a stub would have been: this service was witnessed against a REAL POSTGRESQL 16, initdb'd in this container on port 5433 and migrated with the repository's own packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql. A witness account was created and signed in through apps/web's own /api/auth/sign-in/email at an independent production server, and the cookie that produced was then used against the backend running as a separate process in NODE_ENV=production. Observed: (1) no cookie -> 401 with error not_authenticated; (2) that cookie -> the contract's own {outcome:unavailable, reasons:[{code:provider_not_configured}]} at 503, which is the acceptance's 'deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider' and is byte-identical in shape to what the web target answers in the same condition; (3) DELETE FROM session, then the SAME cookie -> 401 on the very next request, which is PL-0401's database-sessions ruling and the declined cookieCache holding on this side of the boundary; (4) a forged cookie value -> 401, byte-identical to (1); (5) a forged x-liberty-development-account header against the deployment -> never an identity; (6) the 401 body identical across contentId values aurora-fall, invented-title and zzz, which is the non-leaking requirement observed on a live socket rather than only in a unit test. Separately, in a development runtime with the fixture provider, the same service issued a real granted session for aurora-fall with three ranked candidates and the full reason trail -- the decision is the application's own, running here. The service also refused to start at all with no transport stated, and answered 404 on every path but its one route and 405 on a GET to it.

message:
PW-0102: the redundant inner #![cfg(windows)] is removed from apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/windows_host.rs, on the commander's round-90 instruction, WHILE THE TASK IS IN REVIEW. Three things about that are worth stating rather than leaving to be noticed.

WHY IT WAS SAFE TO REMOVE. lib.rs already gates the module: #[cfg(windows)] sits directly above pub mod windows_host;. A module that is not declared cannot be reached, so the inner attribute could only ever be evaluated in a build where it was already true. Removing it changes no build configuration; it removes a second statement of one fact. The header comment now says where the single gate lives and says not to add the attribute back, because a reader who sees no cfg in the file is exactly the person who would re-add one.

WHAT I VERIFIED, AND WHAT I DID NOT. Verified here: cargo check --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc clean; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings clean; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings clean on the host; cargo test --locked 42 passed, 0 failed -- the same 42 as before the edit. NOT verified: that this is the defect the Windows workflow actually reported. gh is not installed in this container and there is no other path to the run's logs from here, so I could not read the failing step. THIS CORRECTIVE IS THE COMMANDER'S DIAGNOSIS, APPLIED, NOT MINE, and I am not claiming to have reproduced the failure. If the workflow still fails after this, the log is the thing to read and the next corrective should come from it rather than from another guess.

WHY THE TASK IS STILL IN REVIEW RATHER THAN BACK IN IN_PROGRESS. The correct lifecycle for a corrective is CHANGES_REQUESTED, which returns a task to IN_PROGRESS and preserves its gate results. assertReviewAllowed refuses it: task.reviewAgent is gpt-architect, and the rule is that a task requiring independent review may not have a review recorded by anyone else -- no automatic substitution. So recording the commander's instruction as a CHANGES_REQUESTED would have meant typing it under gpt-architect's name, which is the reviewer-impersonation PL-AI-0012 exists to prevent, for a convenience. The alternative, release, discards gate results and would have destroyed PW-0102's recorded typecheck, lint and unit passes to save a lifecycle nicety. So the task stays in REVIEW, its implementation tree has moved, and this event is the disclosure: review-status will show a different tree hash from the one gpt-architect was handed, and the reviewer should read the corrected file rather than the round-88 one. The build gate remains FAIL and is untouched.

evidence: APPROVED at 9a7c1fc176aee38bcc236cb3c24559dd7eef4f03, reviewed against integrated origin. gpt-architect's verdict, transcribed by claude-lead from the commander's relay because the GitHub write integration returns 403 and this reviewer cannot execute the control plane. Architecture properties accepted: artwork identity is an opaque assetRef rather than a URL; the catalog and title contracts carry no artwork URL or origin field; unknown URL-like fields do not survive contract parsing; an artwork reference is required to state its intrinsic dimensions; the browser constructs only a same-origin relative artwork path; resolution is confined to one operator-configured directory; ambiguous duplicate files are refused rather than silently selected; and missing artwork retains the designed fallback instead of becoming a broken surface. The reviewer ruled that this is a published-contract concern, that PW-0401 must not be expanded to solve it, and that PW-0312 owns or coordinates the corrective. The clauses added: an actionable sign-in state for signed-out playback; the not_authenticated versus unavailability distinction preserved rather than collapsed, which is the same ruling PW-0403 received; PW-0401's ordering property -- authenticate before the body is consumed, so content existence cannot leak -- preserved through whatever shape the fix takes; any new reason code or envelope state landed as a DELIBERATE contract change under invariant 5 rather than inferred client-side; and both targets plus the cross-target equivalence tests updated together, because e2e compares whole bodies between them and a one-sided contract change is a failing suite at best and a silent divergence at worst. SEPARATELY, THE next-dev IN-MEMORY FINDING IS RULED NOT A PW-0305 DEFECT and does not reopen it. Under next dev the route handlers and the React Server Components may load separate module instances, so the in-memory repository is not a shared process-wide store across those compilation layers; anything server-rendered from data written through a route handler is invisible in that configuration. It predates PW-0305 and the PostgreSQL-backed behaviour was correctly witnessed. A separate development-runtime task should be filed ONLY IF the product intends no-database local development to support server-rendered reads of data written through API routes. RECORDED BEFORE ANY OF THEM IS WRITTEN, which is the order the third amendment got wrong and which the verdict asked for by name: 'If modifying .github/workflows/ci.yml or shared E2E harness paths requires a surface amendment, derive and record it BEFORE writing those files.' Nothing below has been touched at the time this event is appended.

EVERY ENTRY IS DERIVED FROM A CLAUSE, and the clause is named.

FROM 'Deployment requires authentication but the identity system is not configured -> unavailable / 503. Do NOT continue into content/provider resolution.' -- no new paths. The branch is in playback-session-implementation.ts and its suite is playback-session-authentication.test.ts, both already on this surface. The contract table in docs/API_CONTRACTS.md is on it too and its third row is now wrong, so it changes there.

FROM 'PostgreSQL service for the production-mode E2E job; repository migration step; auth secret':
 1. .github/workflows/ci.yml -- a postgres service container on the e2e job, a migration step, and DATABASE_URL / LIBERTY_AUTH_SECRET / LIBERTY_AUTH_BASE_URL / LIBERTY_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS on the production run. The development run is NOT given an identity store: case 5 of the required semantics preserves the development identity mechanism, and the way to preserve it is to keep running it.

FROM 'seeded or programmatically created verified test account; sign-in/session establishment fixture; authenticated cookie/header propagation':
 2. e2e/src/identity.ts -- NEW FILE. Creates the account through the application's own /api/auth/sign-up/email and signs in through /api/auth/sign-in/email, so the session under test is a real database-backed Better Auth session rather than a fake this harness minted. It is a new file rather than an addition to fixtures.ts because fixtures.ts is about CONTENT and this is about IDENTITY, and one file that answers both questions is the file nobody can name the purpose of.
 3. e2e/playwright.config.ts -- pins LIBERTY_AUTH_SECRET and the auth base URL / trusted origins on BOTH application servers, under the rule that file already states in capitals: omitting a variable is not a way to say use the default, it is a way to inherit a developer's .env.local into a server whose answers are about to be recorded as a gate result.
 4. e2e/src/env.ts -- an IDENTITY axis beside the existing WEB_MODE, DATABASE_URL and BUILD TARGET axes, read once, so the config and the specs cannot disagree about whether the server under test has an identity system. It also carries a correction that is overdue independently of this round: DEPLOYMENT_PREAMBLE_REFUSAL's comment still says a configured DATABASE_URL leads to authentication_not_configured 'because nothing in apps/web constructs @liberty/auth/server yet'. PW-0403 built that composition root. The constant has been describing an application that no longer exists.

FROM 'The production-mode playback suite should then exercise: signed-out -> 401 unauthenticated; signed-in valid request -> normal playback decision; signed-in malformed request -> 400 request refusal; configured store unavailable -> 503 unavailable; no content-existence leak while signed out. Keep the existing cross-target whole-body equivalence assertions.':
 5. e2e/tests/playback-session.api.spec.ts -- the five cases. The cross-target equivalence assertions live in playback-session.cross-target.api.spec.ts, which is NOT on this surface and is not being changed: 'keep' is satisfied by leaving them alone.

FROM the same clause, CONDITIONALLY:
 6. e2e/tests/progress.api.spec.ts -- DECLARED BECAUSE IT MIGHT MOVE, NOT BECAUSE IT IS KNOWN TO. It asserts the deployment preamble refusal through the DEPLOYMENT_PREAMBLE_REFUSAL constant rather than a literal, so the env.ts correction may carry it with no edit at all. It also asserts EXPECTED_STORAGE_ADAPTER on a request that, with identity configured and no session, is now refused before storage is reported. If it turns out untouched it comes back out, on the PW-0302 precedent this task has already applied three times.

FROM 'All harness variables are prefixed LIBERTY_E2E_. None of them is declared in .env.example' -- docs/E2E.md is where they ARE declared, in a table, along with the two-mode discipline this change alters:
 7. docs/E2E.md.

A FINDING THAT CHANGES HOW ENTRY 1 IS WRITTEN, discovered while testing the migration step rather than assumed. 
> @liberty/persistence@0.1.0 db:migrate
> node ../../scripts/with-root-env.mjs --mode development drizzle-kit migrate

No config path provided, using default 'drizzle.config.ts'
Reading config file '/home/claude/liberty/packages/persistence/drizzle.config.ts'
Error  Please provide required params for Postgres driver:
    [x] url: '' APPLIES NOTHING AND EXITS 0. drizzle-kit migrate reads packages/persistence/migrations/meta/_journal.json to decide what to apply, and that file does not exist -- the first migration was hand-written, as its own header says, so no generate run ever produced a journal. Verified against a live PostgreSQL 16: a fresh database, drizzle-kit migrate, exit 0, zero relations. The repository's documented migration command has never worked. packages/persistence/** is not on this surface and this task will not fix it; the CI step will apply the migration SQL directly and ASSERT THE TABLES EXIST afterwards, so a silent no-op cannot recur, with a comment naming the defect and the task it is filed against. The defect is being filed as its own proposal for gpt-architect.

ONE CONFIGURATION CHOICE THAT SHOULD BE RULED ON RATHER THAN BURIED. The harness will set LIBERTY_AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=false on the production e2e server. Sign-up otherwise answers token:null -- which is requireEmailVerification working correctly -- and the only ways to get a session from there are a mail transport, which the composition root deliberately refuses to fake because a verification URL is a one-click account takeover, or a direct UPDATE on the user table, which needs a database driver this harness does not have and would mean the suite reaching around the application it is testing. The account, the sign-in and the session stay entirely real and database-backed; the one precondition relaxed is the one that cannot be satisfied without a mail transport, and it is not what these five cases measure. The verification policy itself is asserted where it belongs, in auth-ui.test.tsx and auth-policy.ts.

CONFLICT CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Every entry is covered only by tasks in a terminal state: .github/workflows/ci.yml by PL-0001, PL-0704 and PL-AI-0002, all DONE; docs/E2E.md by PL-0002, PL-0704, PL-AI-0002 and PL-0706, all DONE, and PL-0703, SUPERSEDED; e2e/** by PL-0501, PL-0701, PL-0105 and PL-0706, all DONE. PW-0501, which gpt-architect asked to proceed in parallel, holds .github/workflows/windows.yml, apps/desktop/** and scripts/windows/** and overlaps none of this -- so the two are conflict-free and may be claimed concurrently, which is the condition the verdict attached to 'Do not wait for PW-0312'.

The task.definition_changed event appended immediately before this one is CORRUPTED and must not be read as written. Its fourth-amendment content is otherwise correct; one paragraph has foreign text spliced into it.

WHAT HAPPENED. The message was passed to the CLI inside DOUBLE quotes and contained a shell backtick pair around a command name. Bash evaluated it as command substitution, actually ran the migration command against an unconfigured environment, and substituted that command's stdout and stderr into the audit record. The paragraph beginning "A FINDING THAT CHANGES HOW ENTRY 1 IS WRITTEN" therefore reads, mid-sentence, as drizzle-kit output complaining about an empty url, where it should say that the repository's documented migration command applies nothing and exits 0.

THE FINDING ITSELF IS UNCHANGED AND WAS ESTABLISHED SEPARATELY, before that event was written, against a live PostgreSQL 16 instance: a fresh database, drizzle-kit migrate run with a real DATABASE_URL, exit 0, and zero relations afterwards. The accidental run captured in the corrupted text is a DIFFERENT invocation with no url at all, and proves nothing either way. The amendment is re-recorded, correctly, in the event that follows this one.

THIRD SHELL-SHAPED MISTAKE THIS PHASE, and the pattern is now worth naming rather than apologising for individually: twice an option-looking string became an event type, and once a backtick became an execution. All three have the same shape -- a long prose message handed to a shell as an argument, where prose punctuation is syntax. The standing remedy for my side is that control-plane messages are written to a file with a quoted heredoc and passed as a single expanded variable, never typed inline; adopted from here.

NOT EDITED OUT. The corrupted event stays exactly as appended. An append-only audit log that gets rewritten when it embarrasses its author is not an audit log, and a reader who finds the splice is better served by this correction beside it than by a clean record that hides a reproducible defect in how these records are produced.

PW-0312 allowedPaths: FIFTH AMENDMENT. Three entries gained, and every one of them was DISCOVERED BY RUNNING THE SUITE rather than predicted. Recorded BEFORE any of the three is written; the observations below come from a run against a live PostgreSQL 16, not from reading the files.

WHY THERE IS A FIFTH AT ALL. The fourth amendment derived the surface from gpt-architect's clauses and got the product side and the harness plumbing right. What it could not derive by reading is which OTHER specs send anonymous requests to a route that now requires an identity. Turning the identity system on in the production run is a change to what the DEPLOYMENT is, not only to what the new tests assert, so every spec that talks to an authenticated route in production mode meets a different answer. The run named them exactly: nine failures across four files, of which two files were already on this surface and two were not.

THE RUN: LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=production with a real database and auth secret, --project=api. 42 passed, 12 skipped, 9 failed. All five of the cases the verdict asked for PASSED, including the signed-out 401, the signed-in decision, the signed-in 400, the forged-cookie 401 and the byte-identical no-leak set. The nine failures are the subject of this amendment.

GAINED.

 1. e2e/src/progress-contract.ts -- THE HARNESS'S RESTATED STATUS MAPPING IS INCOMPLETE, and this is a genuine gap the corrective exposed rather than a consequence of it. `expectedProgressStatus` and `expectedProfilesStatus` both map a `refused` outcome to 403 unless the primary reason is a client-input or conflict code. `not_authenticated` is neither, so the harness demands 403 where the application correctly answers 401 -- which docs/API_CONTRACTS.md has documented as 401 since PW-0403 ("not_authenticated | 401 | the caller. An instance exists and answered; this request carried no valid session"). The mapping was never wrong before because no harness run could reach that state: it needs a deployment with BOTH a store and an auth secret, and until this round no run had one. Three of the nine failures are this, and they are the harness disagreeing with the published contract, not the product.

 2. e2e/tests/rights-boundary.api.spec.ts -- two failures. It posts a media URL smuggled into the session request and requires `denied` / `request_field_not_permitted`. Anonymously, in production, that is now 401 `unauthenticated`, because the gate runs before the body is parsed. THE ASSERTION IS NOT WEAKENED AND MUST NOT BE: the smuggling refusal is a rights property and stays exactly as it is. It is the CALLER that changes -- the request is signed in, so it reaches the schema that refuses it. Asserting a rights refusal against an unidentified caller would be asserting the authentication gate twice under a rights heading.

 3. e2e/tests/playback-session.cross-target.api.spec.ts -- one failure, in "the equivalence table is not vacuously passing on refusals alone". This is the test that stops the whole equivalence table from being two targets that had both simply broken, and its production branch requires both targets to reach the provider gate and name the same operator remedy. Anonymously they now both reach the AUTHENTICATION gate instead -- which is still equivalence, and is the weaker pairing the test's own comment warns about. It is signed in so that the pairing stays what it claims to be. gpt-architect's clause is "Keep the existing cross-target whole-body equivalence assertions"; signing the request in keeps them, and leaving them to compare two 401s would quietly hollow them out.

ALREADY ON THE SURFACE, and changing for the same reason, named here so the diff is not a surprise:

 - e2e/tests/playback-session.desktop.api.spec.ts -- three failures. The forwarder relays the caller's cookie through its IDENTITY_HEADERS allowlist, so a signed-in desktop request reaches the backend as a signed-in one; that is PW-0401's design and this is the first run that can observe it.
 - e2e/tests/progress.api.spec.ts -- the remaining failures are entry 1's, reached through this file.

WHAT IS NOT BEING CHANGED, so that the absence is deliberate rather than overlooked. No product code changes because of any of these nine. Not one of them is the application answering wrongly: in every case the application answers what docs/API_CONTRACTS.md says it should, and the harness was written when no run could reach that answer. If any of the nine had turned out to be the product, it would be a defect and not an expectation to update, and it would be reported as one.

CONFLICT CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. e2e/src/progress-contract.ts is covered by PL-0403 and PL-0501, both DONE; e2e/tests/rights-boundary.api.spec.ts by PL-0701 and PL-0710, both DONE; e2e/tests/playback-session.cross-target.api.spec.ts by PL-0501, DONE. No active task claims any of them. PW-0501 -- which gpt-architect asked to run in parallel -- holds .github/workflows/windows.yml, apps/desktop/** and scripts/windows/** and still overlaps nothing here.

PW-0312 allowedPaths: SIXTH AMENDMENT. One entry: e2e/tests/critical-journey.spec.ts. Recorded BEFORE it is written, and discovered by running the chromium project rather than predicted.

WHAT THE RUN SHOWED. Production mode with a real identity system, --project=chromium: 14 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed, both in critical-journey.spec.ts, both on the watch route:

  - "the watch route answers with the id it was asked about, and never with a src" expects the content id visible on the page and does not find it;
  - "which branch the watch route takes is decided by the build, and both are asserted" waits for a heading matching /available on this deployment/i and does not find it.

WHY, AND IT IS NOT A DEFECT. A signed-out BROWSER on /watch/<id> now reaches the sign-in panel instead of the not-available panel. That is PW-0312 part 1 doing exactly what its acceptance asked for -- "a protected-view redirect or an equivalent actionable signed-out experience" -- and it is the first time any browser-level run in this repository has been able to observe it, because until the identity axis landed no run had a deployment that could tell a signed-out viewer from a signed-in one.

THE THIRD BRANCH IS THE POINT. That test's own name is "both are asserted", and until now there were two branches to assert: a development build mounts the player, a production build shows the not-available panel. There are now three, because "production" has split into "production that can identify a viewer" and "production that cannot". Leaving the test with two branches would mean the configuration CI actually runs is the one nobody asserts -- which is the failure mode that test's name exists to prevent.

WHAT WILL BE WRITTEN. The signed-out branch asserts the sign-in panel and the link that carries the title as the destination, so the clause "reachable FROM the signed-out protected state, not only from a URL somebody knows" is measured in a browser rather than argued from a component test. The other two branches are untouched.

NOT WIDENING FURTHER THAN THAT. No other chromium spec failed. search.spec.ts, the home and title journeys and the skeleton tests all pass unchanged, because none of them is behind an authenticated route.

CONFLICT CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. e2e/tests/critical-journey.spec.ts is covered by PL-0701 and PL-0706, both DONE, and by PL-0703, SUPERSEDED. No active task claims it. PW-0501 still overlaps nothing on this surface.

RUNNING TOTAL, so the growth is visible rather than buried: this task's surface has been amended six times. Amendments one and two were derived before writing; three was not and is recorded as such; four, five and six were. Four, five and six are all consequences of one decision -- giving the harness a real identity system, which gpt-architect's round-93 verdict required in terms -- and each one names the run that produced it. If the reviewer would rather see a single amendment covering e2e/** and .github/workflows/ci.yml wholesale, say so and it will be consolidated; the reason it has not been is that a surface reserved wholesale is a surface nobody can check.

evidence:
turbo run typecheck lint test build at d668fd0: 48 tasks successful, 48 total.

typecheck covers @liberty/web (next build's TypeScript pass, which type-checks the test files too), @liberty/backend, and e2e (tsc --noEmit over the identity axis, the new fixture and six changed specs). lint reports 0 errors and 1 warning -- the pre-existing unused WatchlistEntryRow import in in-memory-repository.test.ts, reported in round 91 and not on this surface. build produces both targets.

WHAT THE TYPES CAUGHT THIS ROUND, because it is the argument for carrying the missing-configuration discriminator in the type rather than in the panel's copy: giving WatchSessionResult's not-configured branch a `missing` field made every construction site and the page's render stop compiling until each said which configuration was absent. The alternative -- leaving the status alone and branching on a reason code inside the page -- would have compiled on the day the second code was added, and gone on printing a sentence about a media provider for a deployment whose provider registry was fine.

Playwright at d668fd0, FOUR configurations, because the identity axis this round added makes "production" two deployments rather than one. All four run sequentially, all four green.

  A. production + identity, --project=api           51 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed
  B. production + identity, --project=chromium      16 passed,  2 skipped, 0 failed
  C. production, NO identity, api + chromium        54 passed, 27 skipped, 0 failed
  D. development,            api + chromium         71 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed

A AND B ARE THE CONFIGURATION CI NOW RUNS, and the one that did not exist before this round. A real PostgreSQL 16 with this repository's own migration applied, a Better Auth instance built by apps/web's composition root, an account created through /api/auth/sign-up/email and a session issued by /api/auth/sign-in/email. Nothing faked.

THE FIVE CASES THE VERDICT NAMED, all in A:
 - signed out -> 401 unauthenticated, reason codes exactly ["not_authenticated"];
 - signed in, valid -> the deployment's real decision (provider_not_configured on a production build), and explicitly NOT an authentication reason: the gate changed WHO gets a decision, not WHAT the decision is;
 - signed in, malformed -> 400 request_malformed, PAIRED IN ONE TEST with the same body sent anonymously getting 401, which is the ordering property observed from outside;
 - a session store consulted about a cookie it has no row for -> 401, driven by a forged token rather than by stopping PostgreSQL, because stopping the database would make the test a statement about the runner;
 - no content-existence leak while signed out -> four bodies a deployment would normally answer four different ways, one set of bytes, and the answer names none of the ids.

B ADDS THE CLAUSE ON SCREEN. "REQUIRED: a sign-in screen reachable FROM the signed-out protected state, not only from a URL somebody knows." A signed-out browser on /watch/<id> gets the sign-in heading, a link whose href is /signin?next=%2Fwatch%2Faurora-fall, and no player element. The locator is scoped to #main because the shell carries its own plain /signin link on every screen -- Playwright's strict mode caught that, and accepting either link would have asserted the weaker one by accident.

C IS THE FAIL-CLOSED CONFIGURATION, and it is asserted rather than skipped away. A production run with no database is now a misconfigured deployment: 503 authentication_not_configured, naming the operator's remedy and not the provider's, with a real title and an invented one answered byte-identically so the refusal cannot be read as a catalog. The 27 skips are honest and carry a sentence: with the route failing closed there is no malformed body to refuse, no device ceiling to apply and no candidate list to compare, so the decision tests skip under PLAYBACK_DECISION_SKIP_REASON rather than asserting the same refusal ten more times under other headings.

D IS CASE 5, PRESERVED BY BEING RUN. The development identity mechanism resolves from headers and never consults a session store; nothing about it changed, and the way to keep that true is to keep exercising it. CI's development job is deliberately given no database.

WHAT THE RUNS FOUND, none of which was predicted by reading:
 - nine specs across four files were sending anonymous requests to a route that now requires an identity. Two files were already on this surface, two were not, and both amendments were recorded before those files were written.
 - the harness's own restated status mapping was incomplete: expectedProgressStatus and expectedProfilesStatus mapped every non-input refusal to 403, so they demanded 403 where the application correctly answers 401 for not_authenticated -- which docs/API_CONTRACTS.md has documented since PW-0403. No run could reach that state before, so the gap had never cost anything. The harness was wrong, not the product.
 - two progress tests asserted the literal "unavailable" for the deployment preamble refusal. Correct for both configurations this harness could previously produce, wrong the moment a third existed. Both now derive the outcome from the same expression as the reason.
 - Better Auth's rate limiter answered the fourth sign-in of a run with 429. It was right. The fixture memoises one sign-in per worker and waits once on a 429, which is obeying a protocol requirement rather than the test retry playwright.config.ts forbids -- no assertion is retried, and the alternative was switching off a real rate limiter to measure a different control.

WITNESSED LIVE OUTSIDE PLAYWRIGHT, against PostgreSQL 16 and a real Better Auth instance, next start under NODE_ENV=production:
 - no DATABASE_URL and no LIBERTY_AUTH_SECRET: a VALID request for a real title answers HTTP 503, outcome unavailable, code authentication_not_configured, cache-control no-store -- and an invented title and a malformed body produce the same bytes by md5. Before this round that same request reached the resolver and answered provider_not_configured.

message:
TWO TASKS CREATED UNOWNED AS PROPOSALS FOR gpt-architect, round 93. Neither is claimed; both follow the PW-0501 precedent of making a proposal machine-readable rather than leaving it in prose.

PL-AI-0014 -- "An option-looking event type is a usage error, not an event". Lane Coordination, P2, surface scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs and scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs.

ROUTED HERE BY THE VERDICT: "File/route it to the task that owns scripts/**, with acceptance that option-looking event types beginning with '-' are refused before append." There is no OPEN task that owns scripts/** -- PL-0003, PL-AI-0001 and PL-AI-0002 all do and all are DONE -- so routing it meant creating one rather than reopening a completed task, which would have discarded a recorded review.

The acceptance is the verdict's, with one addition of my own: the test must assert the events file is UNCHANGED rather than merely that the exit code is non-zero. The defect is the WRITE, and an exit code is not that property. Explicitly out of scope, also the verdict's: "Do not edit historical junk events out of the append-only log."

PL-0406 -- "The documented migration command applies nothing and exits 0". Lane Backend, P1, surface packages/persistence/migrations/** and packages/persistence/package.json.

NOT ROUTED BY THE VERDICT -- found by PW-0312 while building the CI migration step gpt-architect asked for, and verified against a live PostgreSQL 16 before being written down: fresh database, drizzle-kit migrate with a real connection string, exit 0, no relations afterwards. drizzle-kit reads packages/persistence/migrations/meta/_journal.json to decide what to apply and that file does not exist, because the first migration was hand-written -- as its own header says, and says why.

P1 rather than P2 because it is load-bearing in a way it was not before this round: CI's e2e job now needs a migrated database to exercise authenticated playback. That job applies the SQL with psql and then COUNTS THE TABLES, with a comment naming this task, and the count should outlive the fix -- it is cheap, and it is the assertion that would have caught this in the first place.

WHAT NEITHER TASK IS. Neither is a request for a general CLI argument parser, and neither is a request to regenerate the migration from the schema: doing that to obtain a journal would discard the reasoning in a file PL-0405 reviewed as a whole.
