DEFECT, REPRODUCED TWICE ON A RUNNING SERVER: the in-memory repository is instantiated TWICE in a
Next app, once per module graph, so nothing written through /api/v1/* is visible to any server
component and nothing a server component writes is visible to a route handler. It is PRE-EXISTING
and NOT caused by PW-0304; PW-0304 is the first surface whose failure is visible to a reader.

WHERE IT IS. `apps/web/src/lib/db/index.ts:161` caches the chosen repository in a module-level
`let cached`, and `apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.ts:207-212` builds its four `Map`s at
construction. Neither is reachable through `globalThis`. Next's app router compiles the React Server
Components graph and the SSR/route-handler graph as SEPARATE module graphs, so a module-level
binding is per-graph: `createInMemoryRepository()` runs once in each, and the two sets of Maps never
meet. PostgreSQL is unaffected because its state is a database outside the process, which is exactly
why this has been invisible.

HOW IT WAS FOUND. PW-0304's `/watchlist` renders "Choose who is watching" for a session that HAS
selected a profile -- while the profile badge in the same page's topbar, which is a CLIENT component
reading `/api/v1/profiles`, shows the profile by name on the same screen.

REPRODUCTION 1 -- PW-0304, server component vs route handler.
  $ npm run dev --workspace @liberty/web -- --port 3188     # DATABASE_URL and LIBERTY_AUTH_SECRET both empty
  $ curl -s -X POST localhost:3188/api/v1/profiles  -H 'x-liberty-development-account: dbg-acct-1' \
      -H 'x-liberty-development-session: dbg-acct-1-session' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"displayName":"Dbg","avatarKey":null,"maxRating":null}'
    -> 201, profile 45fa84a2-a633-484c-8a83-c6668ef22ce5
  $ curl ... POST /api/v1/profiles/selection -d '{"profileId":"45fa84a2-..."}'
    -> {"outcome":"selected", ...}
  $ curl ... PUT /api/v1/watchlist/aurora-fall -d '{}'
    -> 200
  $ curl ... GET /api/v1/watchlist
    -> {"outcome":"listed", ... "1 entr(y|ies) on this profile's list" ...}
  $ curl ... GET /watchlist          # the PAGE, same headers, same process
    -> renders "Choose who is watching"
  The route handler sees a selected profile and one entry. The server component, one request later,
  sees `session.activeProfileId === null`.

REPRODUCTION 2 -- PW-0305's CONTINUE-WATCHING RAIL, WHICH IS ALREADY DONE AND IS ALSO AFFECTED.
  Same server, account `cw-acct`, profile created and selected as above.
  $ curl ... POST /api/v1/progress/aurora-fall/lease -d '{"writerId":"dbg"}'   -> {"outcome":"leased", epoch 1}
  $ curl ... PUT  /api/v1/progress/aurora-fall \
      -d '{"lease":{"epoch":1,"writerId":"dbg"},"writeSeq":1,"positionSeconds":600,"runtimeSeconds":7680}'
    -> {"outcome":"written", positionSeconds 600, runtimeSeconds 7680}
  600 of 7680 seconds is comfortably `resumable` by `continueWatchingVerdict` -- past
  RESUMABLE_MINIMUM_SECONDS, nowhere near FINISHED_FRACTION.
  $ curl ... GET /   | grep -c "Continue watching"
    -> 0
  The rail is absent. `loadContinueWatching` answers `unavailable` and renders nothing, which is its
  documented behaviour for a refusal -- so the defect is SILENT there. PW-0305's acceptance
  ("a viewer returns and the rail shows what they were watching") cannot be satisfied on any
  in-memory deployment, and nothing reports it.

WHY NOBODY HAD SEEN IT. Every other consumer of the in-memory store is on one side of the split.
`progress.api.spec.ts` and `catalog.api.spec.ts` are wire tests -- route handler to route handler.
The profile picker, the profile badge and the account region are CLIENT components, so their fetches
are route-handler traffic too. `loadContinueWatching` is the only pre-existing server-component read
of profile-scoped state, and it is the one designed to render nothing rather than report a failure.
`loadResumePosition` is a second one, with the same silent `null`.

SCOPE OF THE CLAIM, STATED EXACTLY.
  - OBSERVED: `next dev` (Turbopack), Next 16.3.1, in-memory adapter. Twice, as above.
  - EXPECTED BUT UNVERIFIED: the same split in a production build. The RSC/SSR graph separation is a
    property of the app router's build rather than of dev mode, so a `next build` deployment with no
    DATABASE_URL should behave identically. NOT measured, and must not be reported as measured.
  - NOT AFFECTED: any deployment with a DATABASE_URL. The Postgres repository holds no state in the
    process, so both graphs read the same rows. This is why the product's real configuration hides
    it, and why the harness's production-with-identity axis would not have caught it either.

REMEDY, FOR A RULING RATHER THAN APPLIED HERE. `lib/db/index.ts` and `lib/db/in-memory-repository.ts`
are PW-0305's allowedPaths and are not on PW-0304's surface. The smallest honest fix is to key both
the resolution cache and the in-memory store off a `globalThis` symbol, which is the one module
identity shared across graphs; the alternative -- declaring that the in-memory adapter is
route-handler-only and forbidding server components from reading profile-scoped state -- is a
product decision, not a refactor, and would delete `/watchlist`'s list and the continue-watching
rail as currently designed.

WHAT PW-0304 DOES ABOUT IT IN THE MEANTIME. Nothing that hides it. The server-side read stays,
because it is correct against the adapter the product ships with and because moving the read to the
client would (a) require JavaScript to see your own list, (b) limit the titles it can NAME to
whatever `/api/v1/catalog/home` happens to carry, and (c) be a design chosen to route around another
module's bug. `e2e/tests/watchlist.spec.ts` asserts every part of the journey the route-handler layer
owns -- which is the add control, the optimistic flip, the real refusal and the rollback -- and
states, as a skip reason rather than an omission, that the LIST PAGE's contents can only be asserted
where the two graphs share a store.

message:
PW-0313 PROPOSED, unowned, BACKLOG, awaiting a gpt-architect ruling.

"The in-memory store is two stores: server components and route handlers never share one."

It is the task for the defect recorded as `defect.found` earlier this round, which was found while
building PW-0304 and reproduced twice on a running server. It is filed rather than fixed in place
for two reasons, both of which are gpt-architect's to settle rather than mine:

1. THE REMEDY IS ON ANOTHER TASK'S SURFACE. `apps/web/src/lib/db/index.ts` and
   `in-memory-repository.ts` are PW-0305's allowedPaths. PW-0305 is DONE, so nothing is made stale
   by a new task owning them -- but PW-0304 is in REVIEW and widening ITS surface to reach into
   another feature's storage layer would be scope creep of exactly the kind the surface discipline
   exists to prevent.

2. THERE ARE TWO HONEST REMEDIES AND ONE OF THEM IS A PRODUCT DECISION. Keying the resolution cache
   and the store off a `globalThis` symbol makes the two graphs share one store, which is the
   smallest fix. Declaring instead that the in-memory adapter is route-handler-only -- that no
   server component may read profile-scoped state -- is also coherent, and it would DELETE
   /watchlist's list and PW-0305's continue-watching rail as currently designed. An implementer
   should not pick between those.

WHY IT IS P1 AND NOT P2. PW-0305 is marked DONE and its acceptance ("a viewer returns and the rail
shows what they were watching") cannot be satisfied on any in-memory deployment. The rail answers
`unavailable` and renders nothing, which is its documented behaviour for a refusal, so the failure
is silent -- a developer running `next dev` sees a product with no continue-watching and no reason
given. That is a completed task whose feature does not work in the configuration every developer
uses.

WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a claim that PW-0305 was approved wrongly. Nothing in its review could
have seen this: every other consumer of the in-memory store is on one side of the split, and the
only two pre-existing server-component readers of profile-scoped state -- `loadContinueWatching`
and `loadResumePosition` -- are both designed to answer silently.

DEPENDENTS TO REPOINT IF IT IS ACCEPTED: none mechanically. `e2e/tests/watchlist.spec.ts` carries
the skip reasons this task would remove, and PW-0305's rail has no e2e coverage to enable yet,
which is why the acceptance asks for it rather than assuming it.

PW-0307 SURFACE AND SEQUENCING FINDING, recorded BEFORE claiming it, per the commitment in the
round-100 handoff. Two of its four REQUIRED clauses reach outside its allowedPaths, and one of
them reaches into a task that is not mine to widen into.

PW-0307 allowedPaths are exactly four files: `components/title/episode-list.tsx`,
`components/title/season-navigation.tsx`, `lib/next-episode.ts`, `lib/next-episode.test.ts`.

CLAUSE BY CLAUSE.

1. "season navigation that does not lose the viewer's place" -- INSIDE THE SURFACE. A client
   selector in `season-navigation.tsx` driven from `episode-list.tsx` needs nothing else. A
   URL-driven selector (`?season=2`) would need `app/title/[titleId]/page.tsx` to read
   searchParams, which is a reviewDependency; the client arrangement is chosen partly for that
   reason and partly because "does not lose the viewer's place" is the argument for not navigating.

2. "the next-episode selection rule is a pure function with its own tests, not logic inside a
   component" -- INSIDE THE SURFACE, and `lib/next-episode.ts` and its test file exist for exactly
   this. It is also the clause with no dependency on anything else, so it is the one being built
   first.

3. "per-episode watched and in-progress state from the progress API" -- INSIDE THE SURFACE BUT
   COLLIDES WITH PW-0313. `EpisodeList` can become an async server component that reads
   `headers()` and loads progress itself, which keeps the change inside `episode-list.tsx`. On any
   build with no DATABASE_URL that read returns nothing, for the reason PW-0313 states: the
   in-memory store is built once per Next module graph and a server component never sees what the
   progress API wrote. So the feature will be CORRECT and UNOBSERVABLE in development, exactly as
   /watchlist's list is. I will not design around it -- the alternative is a client fetch per
   episode or one shared client read, which buys dev visibility at the cost of making a static
   list need JavaScript. It will be stated in the gate evidence and the e2e coverage will carry the
   same skip reason PW-0304's does.

4. "a next-episode affordance at the end of playback" -- OUTSIDE THE SURFACE, AND THE FILE BELONGS
   TO A P0 TASK. The affordance has to render in the player: `player-surface.tsx` line 357 already
   sends `MEDIA_ENDED` into the state machine, so the hook exists, but the player is handed only
   `{session, policy}` and knows nothing about a series. Delivering this clause needs
     - `apps/web/src/components/player/player-surface.tsx`, which is in **PW-0306**'s allowedPaths
       (P0, BACKLOG, "A player that can actually be operated"), and
     - `apps/web/src/app/watch/[contentId]/page.tsx`, to resolve the next episode server-side and
       pass it in. That file is nobody's active surface (PL-AI-0006, PW-0301, PW-0305 and PW-0312
       all own it and all are DONE) and is a reviewDependency of PW-0309, which is READY and
       unclaimed.

   WHY I AM NOT SIMPLY AMENDING INTO IT. gpt-architect's round-99 ruling on the PW-0304 surface was
   "amend the task surface narrowly rather than granting broad `components/title/**`" and the
   stated reason was to keep PW-0307 parallelisable with it. The same reasoning points the other
   way here: taking `player-surface.tsx` would collide with PW-0306 the moment PW-0306 is claimed,
   and PW-0306 is a P0 whose whole subject is that file. An end-of-playback overlay is, on its
   face, a player control -- PW-0306's own acceptance already requires "an idle-hide overlay that
   never hides a control from a keyboard or screen-reader user", which is the same layer.

   PW-0306 is NOT a way out either: it is BLOCKED behind PW-0206 (BACKLOG, "Subtitle and audio
   track selection"), so "wait for PW-0306" means this clause waits on two unstarted tasks.

   THE DECISION IS gpt-architect's, and it is one of three:
     (a) amend PW-0307 to include `player-surface.tsx` and `app/watch/[contentId]/page.tsx`, and
         accept that PW-0306 must then wait for PW-0307's review rather than the reverse;
     (b) move clause 4 to PW-0306 and narrow PW-0307's acceptance to the series surface, with the
         next-episode RULE (clause 2) staying here as the thing PW-0306 would consume; or
     (c) file clause 4 as its own small task depending on PW-0307, owning those two files, so
         neither of the two bigger tasks blocks the other.
   I have no preference I would defend. (b) and (c) both leave PW-0307 completable now; (a) does
   not, because it would make a P0 wait.

WHAT I AM DOING IN THE MEANTIME. Claiming PW-0307 and building clauses 1, 2 and 3. The task will
NOT be moved to REVIEW with clause 4 unaddressed -- an acceptance with a REQUIRED clause nobody
delivered is not satisfied, and marking it DONE would be the exact thing the operating contract
forbids. It stays IN_PROGRESS with this finding as the reason, in the same way PW-0107 is
IN_PROGRESS waiting on a Windows run.

write, collision and staging surface. reviewDependencies is read-only and WIDENS ONLY WHAT AN
APPROVAL FINGERPRINTS." Widening the fingerprint is the entire mechanism -- a reviewDependency
exists so that a change under it invalidates an approval. Writing into another task's
reviewDependency while that task is in REVIEW is therefore not a near-miss; it is the exact event
the field was added to catch. It caught it.

THE RULE I SHOULD HAVE BEEN APPLYING, written down so the next conflict check uses it: a candidate
path conflicts with a live task if it appears in that task's allowedPaths (a write collision) OR in
its reviewDependencies (a fingerprint collision). Both. The second one is the easier to miss
precisely because nothing is being written there, and "I am only adding a file next to it" is not a
defence -- `season-navigation.module.css` and `season-navigation.test.tsx` are new files that

an approval at a commit the reviewer did not name would be me deciding what they reviewed, which is

message:
A WRITTEN ACCESSIBILITY INVARIANT AND THE SHIPPED PAGE NOW DISAGREE, and the resolution is a design
position rather than a repair, so it is filed instead of applied.

`apps/web/src/components/search/search-form.tsx:421` does not describe the search surface, it rules
on it:

    THE live region for this surface -- one, singular, and the page must not add another.

PW-0304 added another, and not by oversight: `watchlist-control.tsx` renders a `role="status"`
notice per control, always present and usually empty, because -- its own words -- "a live region
inserted at the moment it gains content is a live region some screen readers never announce,
because they were not watching the node when it appeared." The search RESULTS are catalog cards and
every routable one now carries a control. A query matching eight titles puts nine polite live
regions on that page.

WHY THIS IS NOT BEING FIXED BY ME, EITHER WAY.

  - Deleting the control's region would remove the only channel by which a screen-reader user
    learns that a watchlist write was REFUSED. That is the clause PW-0304 exists for, and the
    defect shape the acceptance says "the harnesses in this repository have caught four times".
  - Rewriting `search-form.tsx`'s comment to narrow its own rule is a change to a documented
    accessibility position on a file that is on no live task's surface, made by the person whose
    work broke it. That is the kind of edit that should be somebody else's call.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT KNOWN ABOUT THE USER IMPACT, stated honestly because I cannot measure it here.
Multiple `aria-live="polite"` regions are valid ARIA and are routine on real pages; the queue is
per-page and serialised, so they do not talk over each other. The watchlist notices are EMPTY
except in the moment after that viewer pressed that specific control, so in ordinary use exactly
one region ever has content. What I have NOT done is test it with a screen reader -- there is none
in this container -- so "harmless" is an argument, not a measurement, and it should not be recorded
as one.

THE OPTIONS, for a ruling:
  (a) narrow the rule in `search-form.tsx` to what it is actually defending -- one region that
      describes the RESULT SET -- and note that per-control notices are a different kind of
      message. Cheapest, and in my view the true statement.
  (b) give the watchlist notice `role="alert"` instead, so it is not a second polite region. I
      would argue against it: assertive interrupts, and `search-form.tsx` itself records why that
      was wrong for the error panel ("an assertive region interrupts a polite one").
  (c) have the control render its notice only when non-empty and accept the announcement risk its
      header documents. Also arguably wrong, and it is the arrangement PW-0304 deliberately
      rejected.

A real screen-reader pass on the search results page would settle it better than any of the three
arguments above, and nothing in this environment can perform one.

message:
PW-0313 surface: `e2e/tests/watchlist.spec.ts` MOVED FROM reviewDependencies TO allowedPaths, now
that PW-0304 is DONE. This is the amendment gpt-architect's round-102 ruling instructed: "Because
watchlist.spec.ts sits inside PW-0304's reviewed surface, wait until PW-0304 reaches DONE before
touching it. Then amend PW-0313's allowedPaths narrowly to include that exact file if necessary."

It was necessary. PW-0313's last outstanding evidence item is item 5: "the skipped development
watchlist assertions in watchlist.spec.ts become executable rather than being deleted." They are
assertions in that file; there is no way to enable them from outside it.

WHY IT MOVES RATHER THAN IS ADDED. It is already a PW-0313 reviewDependency. Leaving it in both
fields would be declaring the same path read-only and writable at once; `allowedPaths` is the
stronger claim and subsumes the fingerprint effect, since a task's own writes are fingerprinted
anyway. One field, one meaning.

WHAT WILL CHANGE IN IT, so this is not a blank cheque. The file's header currently states, as a
documented limitation, that configuration C -- a development build -- "cannot observe the LIST PAGE
at all", and groups C's write assertions read the API back instead of the page because the page
could not see the write. PW-0313 removes that limitation. The edit is therefore: correct the
header so it stops describing a defect that no longer exists, and add the list-page assertions to
the development group that were impossible before. NOTHING IS DELETED -- the wire-level
`listedContentIds` checks stay, because "the server agrees with the row" and "the page agrees with
the server" are two different claims and the second does not imply the first.

CONFLICT CHECK, BOTH FIELDS, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Live tasks are PW-0307 (IN_PROGRESS: episode-list.tsx,
season-navigation.*, lib/next-episode.*), PW-0107 (IN_PROGRESS: .github/workflows/windows.yml,
scripts/windows/**) and PW-0313 itself. `e2e/tests/watchlist.spec.ts` is in neither of the other
two's allowedPaths nor in their reviewDependencies. PW-0304, which held it, reached DONE earlier
this round, so nothing live can be made stale by writing to it -- which is the whole reason this
amendment waited.

A LOAD-DEPENDENT TEST IN `critical-journey.spec.ts`, DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN RETRIED. It failed on the
development chromium run for PW-0313 and it is the same defect class as PL-0706: a result that
depends on how busy the machine is, not on the product.

THE FAILURE:

  [chromium] critical-journey.spec.ts:520 > the play affordance is offered only where a rights
  basis can be read, and both are asserted                                               (12.0s)
  Error: expect(page).toHaveURL(expected) failed
    Expected pattern: /\/watch\/aurora-fall$/
    Received string:  "http://127.0.0.1:3177/title/aurora-fall"
    Timeout: 10000ms

THE CAUSE, FROM THE SERVER LOG RATHER THAN FROM A GUESS. The web server's own output straddles the
failure:

  [WebServer] (c) Compiling /watch/[contentId] ...
    (x) 9 [chromium] ... the play affordance ...                                         (12.0s)
  [WebServer]  GET /watch/aurora-fall 200 in 262ms (next.js: 48ms, ...)

The click DID navigate. Next's client router issued `GET /watch/aurora-fall?_rsc=...` and that
request sat waiting while Turbopack compiled the route for the first time. `/watch/[contentId]`
pulls shaka-player, which is the heaviest chunk in this application. The 262ms logged afterwards is
the SERVE time, not the compile; the compile is the line above it, and it outlasted the 10-second
`expect` timeout. On the previous round's run the same compile was inside the request and logged as
`200 in 6.8s (next.js: 6.6s)` -- and that run PASSED, in 8.1s, with under two seconds of margin.

WHY IT TIPPED OVER NOW, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT WAS MY WORK THAT DID IT. This round added
`e2e/tests/continue-watching.spec.ts` and four `/watchlist` navigations to `watchlist.spec.ts`.
This container has two cores and the suite runs one worker; more routes compiled earlier in the run
means more contention when `/watch` finally compiles. I did not introduce the dependence on load,
but I consumed the margin that was hiding it.

IT IS NOT A PRODUCT DEFECT, and that was checked rather than assumed. Driven by hand against a dev
server with a 2.5s settle before the click, the whole sequence works: `[nav]
http://127.0.0.1:3240/watch/aurora-fall`, the player mounts, Shaka requests
`https://fixtures.invalid/aurora-fall/manifest.mpd` and fails on DNS exactly as it should with no
media rig configured. `curl` to the same route answers 200 in 304ms cold and 87ms warm.

THE FIX, WHICH IS A STRENGTHENING AND NOT A RAISED CEILING. `expect(page).toHaveURL()` polls an
assertion with the `expect` timeout -- a constant chosen for assertions about values, applied here
to a wait on a BUILD. The semantically correct wait is `page.waitForURL()`, which waits for the
navigation and is bounded by the test timeout; the URL assertion stays after it, so the test still
asserts exactly what it asserted before and now fails for the right reason when it fails.
PL-0706's acceptance is explicit that "A RAISED testTimeout IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE FIX ON ITS OWN:
it moves the ceiling without removing the dependence on disk state". Raising `expect.timeout`
globally would be that move; waiting on the navigation removes the dependence instead.

SCOPE, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `grep -rn toHaveURL e2e/tests/` finds three. The two in
`search.spec.ts` assert a query-string change on a route that is already compiled -- no new route,
no compile, and that file says so itself ("Waits on the URL, not on the debounce"). This is the
only one that crosses a first compile of a heavy route.

PW-0313 allowedPaths: ONE FILE ADDED, before it is edited.

ADDED: e2e/tests/critical-journey.spec.ts

WHY IT IS THIS TASK'S TO FIX. PW-0313's `e2e` gate is the full project, not one spec -- that lesson
was learned the hard way on PW-0304 this round, where running only the file I had written let a
regression reach an approval. A load-dependent test anywhere in that project makes the gate
unrecordable honestly: I would be reporting a number that a slower machine would not reproduce. The
diagnosis is the `defect.found` recorded immediately before this.

It is also this round's work that consumed the margin the flake was hiding behind, which is stated
in that event. The test was already load-dependent; `continue-watching.spec.ts` and four extra
`/watchlist` navigations are what pushed a cold Turbopack compile of `/watch/[contentId]` past the
10-second `expect` ceiling.

WHAT WILL CHANGE: one assertion. `await expect(page).toHaveURL(re)` becomes
`await page.waitForURL(re)` followed by the same `expect(page).toHaveURL(re)`. Nothing is deleted
and nothing is relaxed -- the test asserts the same URL and now waits on the navigation rather than
polling an assertion timeout at a build.

WHAT WILL NOT CHANGE: `playwright.config.ts`'s `expect: { timeout: 10_000 }`, `timeout: 60_000` and
`retries: 0`. Raising any of them is the move PL-0706's acceptance names as unacceptable on its own
-- "it moves the ceiling without removing the dependence" -- and `retries` is the one number this
harness exists to keep at zero.

CONFLICT CHECK, BOTH FIELDS, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Live tasks are PW-0307 (IN_PROGRESS:
components/title/episode-list.tsx, season-navigation.*, lib/next-episode.*), PW-0107 (IN_PROGRESS:
.github/workflows/windows.yml, scripts/windows/**) and PW-0313 itself.
`e2e/tests/critical-journey.spec.ts` is in neither of the other two's allowedPaths nor in their
reviewDependencies. Its historical owners -- PL-0501, PL-0701, PL-0704, PL-0706, PW-0312 and
PL-0703 -- are DONE or SUPERSEDED, and PW-0601, which lists `e2e` as a reviewDependency, is DONE.
Nothing live can be made stale.

THE PLAYER CRITICAL PATH IS LONGER THAN THE ROUND-103 RULING STATES, AND IT TERMINATES IN A
HARDWARE EXPERIMENT ONLY THE COMMANDER CAN RUN. PW-0206 cannot be claimed, and neither can anything
between it and the bottom.

WHAT THE RULING SAID: "The current dependency chain is now: PW-0206 -> PW-0306 -> final clause of
PW-0307. PW-0206 is BACKLOG and unowned. PW-0306 is BACKLOG and unowned. ... Proceed in dependency
order where the control plane permits: 1. claim and implement PW-0206."

THE CONTROL PLANE DOES NOT PERMIT IT. Three attempts, three refusals:

    $ npm run ai:claim -- PW-0206 claude-frontend
    AI control plane error: PW-0206 is BACKLOG, not READY
    $ npm run ai:claim -- PW-0205 claude-frontend
    AI control plane error: PW-0205 is BACKLOG, not READY
    $ npm run ai:claim -- PW-0204 claude-frontend
    AI control plane error: PW-0204 is BACKLOG, not READY

THE ACTUAL CHAIN, walked from the task graph rather than from memory:

    PW-0307 (final clause)
      PW-0306  BACKLOG  P0  A player that can actually be operated
        PW-0206  BACKLOG  P1  Subtitle and audio track selection
          PW-0202  DONE
          PW-0205  BACKLOG  P0  NativePlayerAdapter translates mpv into the state machine
            PW-0201  DONE
            PW-0204  BACKLOG  P0  libmpv in the shell: a child HWND, gpu-next, an event pump
              PW-0102  DONE
              PW-0103  BLOCKED P0  Experiment 1a: can a child HWND composite beneath the webview

So the ruling's three-link chain is really six, and the bottom link is BLOCKED -- not by capacity,
not by a surface collision, and not by anything this session can arrange. PW-0103 needs a Windows
machine with a GPU and a display. `coordination/LAST_MILE.md` item 7 has said so since it was
written, and the control plane's own blocked reason says it: "Requires the commander's real Windows
hardware, which no agent in this session can reach."

WHY THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS ROUND'S HANDOFF. The ruling calls this path "one of the
highest-impact remaining product paths", and it is -- the product cannot play anything with
operable controls until PW-0306, and PW-0306 cannot start until the native engine exists. Every one
of those tasks is waiting on an experiment that has never been run, and LAST_MILE item 7 states the
stake plainly: the whole choice of Tauri rests on it, so a FAILURE reverses decision D1 rather than
being worked around. The project has four P0 tasks parked behind a question nobody has answered.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING. Not unblocking PW-0103 -- the hardware fact has not changed. Not moving
PW-0204, PW-0205 or PW-0206 to READY by editing their dependencies, which would be bypassing the
graph to look productive, and which the ruling forbids in terms: "Do not bypass the dependency
graph just to finish PW-0307 sooner." Not claiming PW-0206 by any other route.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY MOVE IT, in the order the graph implies:
  1. the commander runs Experiment 1a on real Windows hardware and reports the result; or
  2. gpt-architect rules that some part of PW-0204 can be established without it -- for instance
     the event pump and the invoke boundary, which are software, as against the compositing
     question, which is not; or
  3. gpt-architect re-scopes PW-0205/PW-0206 so the WEB engine's half can land first. PW-0206's own
     acceptance requires "one normalised track vocabulary that BOTH adapters answer in", so a
     web-only half would need that clause narrowed deliberately rather than quietly satisfied.
Option 3 is the only one available to this session, and it is a scope decision rather than
implementation.

PW-0208 ("An LGPL-compatible libmpv and FFmpeg the product may actually ship") is READY and is NOT
on this chain -- PW-0204 depends on PW-0102 and PW-0103, not on PW-0208 -- so claiming it would not
shorten the path by one link. It is also a `build` gate for a Windows binary this container cannot
produce.

WHAT I AM DOING INSTEAD, under "continue with the next dependency-clear high-impact work rather
than stopping": PW-0309, "Offline, degraded and error states a desktop application needs" -- P1,
READY, dispatchable to claude-frontend, frontend work that needs no Windows and no native engine.

ADDED:
  apps/web/src/components/shell/app-shell.tsx      -- so the degraded state is actually visible
  e2e/tests/degraded-states.spec.ts        (new)   -- so the `e2e` gate has something to run

WHY THE SHELL. The acceptance requires "a visible degraded mode that names what is unavailable". A
banner nobody mounts is not visible. `app-shell.tsx` is the one place every route in this
application renders through -- that is what PW-0301 built it for -- and an offline state that
appeared on some routes and not others would be a worse lie than none. The edit is one element
inside the existing `<main>` region; `AppShell` already opens two client boundaries
(`AccountRegion`, `ActiveProfileBadge`) for exactly this kind of browser-side fact, so this adds no
new architectural seam.

ONE NAMED FILE, NOT `components/shell/**`. That wildcard would also take `navigation.ts` and
`shell-usage.test.ts`, neither of which this task has any reason to touch.

WHY AN e2e SPEC. `e2e` is a required gate here and the task's surface named no spec file -- the
same gap PW-0304 and PW-0307 both hit. It is also the only layer that can exercise this at all:
the states are produced by the browser losing its network, and Playwright's
`context.setOffline(true)` is a real offline condition rather than a stub. `apps/web` runs Vitest
in a `node` environment with no DOM, so no unit test here can take a page offline.

AND A DESIGN DECISION WORTH RECORDING WITH THE AMENDMENT, because it is why no third file is
needed: THIS TASK ADDS NO PROBE AND NO NEW ROUTE. `/api/health` is deliberately liveness-only --
its own header says "every fact added to it is a fact published to everyone" -- so the backend's
reachability will NOT be bolted onto it. The three states are instead derived from what the
application's own requests already report:

  - a same-origin request that fails at the TRANSPORT layer while the browser reports itself
    offline            -> the network is down;
  - the same failure while the browser reports itself online
                       -> the sidecar that serves this page did not answer;
  - a request that SUCCEEDS at the transport layer and answers an `unavailable` envelope naming
    `provider_unavailable`
                       -> the backend is down.

That third distinction is not invented here either. `playbackSessionReasonCodeSchema` already
separates them and says why in its own comments: `provider_unavailable` and
`provider_not_configured` "are the operator's and the network's problems", while
`not_authenticated` "is the viewer's, and it is the only reason in this vocabulary whose remedy the
viewer themselves can carry out." The acceptance's "the three have different remedies and
collapsing them produces a support burden" is the same distinction one layer up, so this task
consumes that vocabulary rather than writing a second one.

WHAT FAILED, VERBATIM:

  FAIL src/components/watchlist/watchlist-ui.test.tsx > the screen is reachable
       > the shell renders it as an anchor and marks it current on the route
  Error: invariant expected app router to be mounted
    at useRouter (next/src/client/components/navigation.ts:169)
    at DegradedBanner (src/components/state/degraded-banner.tsx:62)

WHY. PW-0309 mounts `DegradedBanner` inside `AppShell`, and the banner calls `useRouter` so it can
`router.refresh()` when a degraded state clears -- which is the acceptance's "recovery on reconnect
without a manual reload". `useRouter` throws outside a mounted app router, and there is no router
in a `node` vitest process. Any suite that renders `AppShell` with `renderToStaticMarkup` therefore
needs the stub that `profile-ui.test.tsx` and `auth-ui.test.tsx` already carry:

  vi.mock("next/navigation", () => ({ useRouter: () => ({ refresh: () => {} }) }));

FOUR SUITES MENTION `AppShell`; ONLY ONE BREAKS, which is worth stating because it bounds the
amendment. `profile-ui.test.tsx` already mocks the module. `title-styles.test.ts` and
`shell-usage.test.ts` read source rather than rendering the shell. So this is one file and one
`vi.mock` line, not a sweep.

WHY THE COMPONENT KEEPS `useRouter` RATHER THAN THE TEST BEING SPARED. The alternatives are worse.
`window.location.reload()` is the manual reload the acceptance forbids, wearing a function call.
Doing nothing leaves every server component that rendered while the network was down -- "We
couldn't load the catalog", an empty continue-watching rail -- stale on screen after it comes back,
which is exactly the state this task exists to remove. `router.refresh()` re-renders them in place
and is the API for it.

A CONSEQUENCE WORTH NAMING RATHER THAN DISCOVERING LATER: `AppShell` now depends on the app router,
so every future suite that renders it needs that stub. Three of the four already do or do not
render it, so the cost today is one line -- but it is a new obligation on a component every route
goes through, and it belongs in the record rather than in somebody's afternoon.

message: ROUTER REFRESH CAN DESTROY THE APPLICATION OFFLINE, AND IT IS NOT ONLY PW-0309'S PROBLEM. PW-0208 STOP AND REPORT: SHIPPING AN H.264 OR HEVC DECODER NEEDS PATENT LICENCES THIS PROJECT DOES NOT HOLD. The task's own acceptance instructs this: 'NOT IN SCOPE: any decoder whose distribution needs a patent licence this project does not hold -- if one is required, stop and report it as a commander decision rather than shipping it.' One is required, so the work stopped at the boundary instead of choosing. COPYRIGHT AND PATENTS ARE INDEPENDENT. An LGPL FFmpeg built exactly as docs/LICENSING.md section 2 specifies is correctly licensed under copyright law and says nothing about patents; ffmpeg.org/legal.html declines to advise -- 'We do not know, we are not lawyers so we are not qualified to answer this' -- while warning that patent holders pursue fees once a product earns money. AVC/H.264: Via LA's programme covers decoders incorporated into products distributed to end users, which is what shipping libmpv-2.dll inside a desktop application is. Published Codec Products schedule: 0.00 USD for the first 100,000 units per year per affiliated legal entity, 0.20 USD per unit to 5,000,000, 0.10 USD beyond, with an annual enterprise cap. The zero is a RATE, not an absence of a licence, and that distinction is counsel's to resolve rather than this task's. HEVC/H.265: structurally worse -- patents are split across Via LA's HEVC/VVC programme, Access Advance's HEVC Advance pool and unpooled holders, so no single licence clears it, and Access Advance's published rates changed effective 2026-07-01. THE THREE OPTIONS, stated without a recommendation: (1) ship both decoders and obtain the licences; (2) ship neither and fall back to the platform's Media Foundation decoders for those two codecs, which moves the patent position to Microsoft's per-machine licensing and costs the format coverage that motivated libmpv; (3) ship a royalty-free-only build (AV1, VP9, Opus, Vorbis, FLAC) and accept what that excludes. NOTHING WAS DISABLED ON A GUESS: no decoder is turned off in the configuration docs/LICENSING.md specifies, because the choice is a product decision with a large cost and it is the commander's and counsel's to make.

message: PL-0713 FILED: e2e/tests/playback-session.desktop.api.spec.ts SHARES ONE MUTABLE LEDGER ACROSS PARALLEL WORKERS, SO IT IS GREEN ON TWO CORES AND RED ON A CI RUNNER. FOUND BY READING THE RUN, NOT BY GUESSING. CI run 37007312900 on d6d0324 failed its e2e job with three annotations, all in that file: development, line 187, 'Expected length: 1 Received length: 0'; production, line 187, 'Expected length: 1 Received length: 2'; production, line 351, 'expect(await ledger()).toHaveLength(1)'. Development 1 failed / 14 skipped / 86 passed; production 2 failed / 25 skipped / 74 passed. The validate job SUCCEEDED in 25m 4s and e2e-typecheck SUCCEEDED in 12s, so the run's single cause is this spec. REPRODUCED LOCALLY AND DIAGNOSED. The stub backend keeps ONE ledger for the whole process; three tests call clearLedger() and then assert the ledger holds exactly their own request. playwright.config.ts sets fullyParallel: true, which splits tests WITHIN a file across workers. This container has 2 cores so Playwright uses 1 worker and they serialise; a CI runner has more, so another test's forwarded request lands between the clear and the read -- 0 when a neighbour cleared after this one posted, 2 when a neighbour posted after this one cleared. Running the file locally with --workers=4 reproduces the exact failure: 1 failed, 8 passed. NOT CAUSED BY THIS ROUND. Neither PW-0309 nor PW-0503 touches that spec, the stub, or the forwarder; d6d0324 is simply the first run after the branch was published. The defect has been latent since the file was written and no previous CI run exercised it with this timing. WHAT THE FIX MUST NOT BE: relaxing toHaveLength(1) to 'at least one'. That assertion is the point -- the spec's own comment says 'a forwarder that retried, or that fanned out, would be taking a decision it has no business taking, and a duplicated session request against a real backend is a duplicated authorization'. Weakening it would delete the check to make the schedule convenient.

PL-0713: TWO CANDIDATE REMEDIES MEASURED, BOTH INSUFFICIENT, AND THE THIRD IS NAMED. Each was applied locally, run, and REVERTED; the working tree carries none of them and e2e/tests/playback-session.desktop.api.spec.ts is byte-identical to HEAD. I cannot claim PL-0713 -- claude-test is the only agent advertising the Test lane, its maxParallel is 1, and PW-0503 holds the slot while it sits in REVIEW -- so this is a handover rather than a fix. The lane is not negotiable to fit capacity: PL-0712, the same class of defect (a repo guard that times out under load), is lane Test. CANDIDATE 1, SCHEDULING: test.describe.configure({ mode: 'default' }) at the top of the file. The file alone passed at --workers=4 and --workers=8, but the whole api project at --workers=4 still failed, and the ledger dump named the polluter -- the same file's own 'a malformed body is refused before it is forwarded to anybody' test, which deliberately forwards four more requests and whose comment says so: 'the forwarder relays the bytes as given, so a malformed body IS forwarded'. The directive did not serialise the file under a fullyParallel project. CANDIDATE 2, SCOPING BY CONTENT ID: replace clearLedger() with a ledgerFor(contentId) that filters the ledger by the id the test sent. Deterministically WORSE -- 2 failures at 1, 4 and 8 workers alike -- because aurora-fall appears in SEVEN requests across this file and northstar in two. Content id is not a unique scope; clearLedger() was what had been keeping the ledger small. CANDIDATE 3, NOT YET TRIED, AND THE ONE I WOULD IMPLEMENT: give each ledger-asserting test a content id that NO other request in the suite uses -- the stub already keys behaviour off contentId (stub-unavailable, stub-redirect, stub-off-contract), so ids like ledger-forwarded and ledger-identity-headers would forward normally and scope the ledger uniquely. Then clearLedger() is deleted, no test mutates shared state, isolation is a property of the request rather than of the machine's core count, and toHaveLength(1) survives unchanged -- which the acceptance requires, because it is the assertion that the forwarder neither retries nor fans out. THE MEASUREMENT THAT MUST ACCOMPANY THE FIX: the whole api project, green at --workers=4 and --workers=8 as well as at 1. A pass at one worker is exactly what hid this.

It aborted at 10m 38s on 30cef6e and at 10m 26s on 2c037d5 -- twelve seconds apart, on two different commits, after passing at 25m 4s and 27m 29s on the two runs before those. Two consecutive aborts at nearly the same elapsed time is not the shape of a flake; it is the shape of a deterministic abort at a particular point in the job. It remains UNDIAGNOSED and no cause is claimed: the annotation names an exit code and no step, and the log needs authentication. PL-0714 was created and implemented this round to make the next occurrence name the step, the machine conditions and, if V8 aborted, what V8 said.

THE e2e FAILURE IS NEW AND IS NOT PL-0713. Production mode only: 1 failed / 75 passed / 31 skipped, on watchlist.spec.ts:859, with 'the harness could not sign in as e2e-watchlist-unchosen-0@liberty.invalid: 401 INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD'. PW-0206's dependency on PW-0205 holds the entire consumer-visible player behind hardware nobody in this session can reach, and the evidence says the dependency is heavier than the work.

THE CHAIN. PW-0307 clause 3 -> PW-0306 -> PW-0206 -> PW-0205 -> PW-0204 -> PW-0103, which is BLOCKED on the commander's Windows machine. So 'play, pause, seek, volume, fullscreen, keyboard operation' -- PW-0306's acceptance, the controls a viewer actually touches, of which this product has NONE -- is gated on an experiment about compositing a child HWND. Three round handoffs have reported this chain as blocked and asked for nothing; round 107's directive says to drive PW-0206, so it was examined rather than reported again.

WHAT PW-0206'S WRITE SURFACE ACTUALLY IS: apps/web/src/components/player/tracks.ts and tracks.test.ts. Two files. A pure module. It writes no adapter -- PW-0205 writes native-player-adapter.ts and native-bridge.ts -- so PW-0206 cannot be consuming PW-0205's code inside its own surface. The acceptance asks for 'one normalised track vocabulary that BOTH adapters answer in', and a vocabulary both adapters answer in is a contract, which is the thing that goes BEFORE an implementation rather than after it. The mpv side of that contract is already specified, in docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 6 -- PW-0205's own acceptance says it implements that section, so the shared source is the document, not the code.

AND PW-0206'S PREMISE SENTENCE IS NOW FACTUALLY OUT OF DATE. It says 'THIS CAPABILITY DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL TODAY: there is no getTextTracks, no selectAudioLanguage, no track state and no UI anywhere in the repository.' Since PW-0201 and PW-0202 landed, apps/web/src/components/player/player-adapter.ts declares PlayerTrack, PlayerTrackKind, getTracks(), selectAudioTrack(), selectSubtitleTrack(), a tracks event and a trackselected event; web-player-adapter.ts implements all of them against Shaka, calling getTextTracks, selectTextTrack, setTextTrackVisibility and selectAudioLanguage. The normalised vocabulary EXISTS. And packages/media-engine already holds the selection policy -- selectAudioTrack, selectSubtitleTrack, withSelectedAudio, languageMatch with the script and macrolanguage rules -- against the contract shapes in packages/contracts/src/domains/audio.ts and subtitles.ts.

SO WHAT IS GENUINELY MISSING IS WHAT THE SURFACE IS FOR: a bridge from the engine-reported PlayerTrack list to the contract shapes the policy consumes, the DEFAULT selection coming from that policy rather than from a second one invented in the player, forced and default flags honoured, and a viewer's explicit choice re-applied after a candidate switch. None of that needs mpv to exist. All of it is pure and testable today.

ACTION TAKEN THIS ROUND, AND HOW TO REVERSE IT: PW-0206 dependencies amended from [PW-0202, PW-0205] to [PW-0202], recorded as task.definition_changed. No acceptance clause was deleted or weakened -- every REQUIRED stands, including 'both adapters answer in', which PW-0205 must then satisfy against what this produces. To reverse: restore PW-0205 to PW-0206's dependencies and release PW-0206. If gpt-architect judges that a track vocabulary must not be fixed before the mpv adapter is written, that is a legitimate call and this finding is the argument against it, not a fait accompli.

PW-0206 dependencies: [PW-0202, PW-0205] -> [PW-0202]. Recorded BEFORE any file is written. The full argument is in this round's board.sequencing_finding; the short form is that PW-0206's write surface is two pure files, the normalised vocabulary it is named for already exists in player-adapter.ts (PW-0201, DONE) and is already implemented against Shaka in web-player-adapter.ts (PW-0202, DONE), the selection policy already exists in packages/media-engine, and PW-0205 writes files PW-0206 does not touch. PW-0205 remains sequenced where it is and must answer in whatever vocabulary this produces.

NO ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE WAS DELETED, WEAKENED OR REWORDED. Every REQUIRED stands verbatim. A dated CORRECTION was appended to the notes recording that the acceptance's premise sentence -- 'there is no getTextTracks, no selectAudioLanguage, no track state and no UI anywhere in the repository' -- stopped being true when PW-0201 and PW-0202 landed, and naming exactly what now exists. Correcting a stale statement of fact is not the same as lowering a bar, and leaving it would have had the implementer either re-building what exists or quietly ignoring the sentence.

CONFLICT-CHECKED IN BOTH FIELDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. PW-0206's allowedPaths are apps/web/src/components/player/tracks.ts and tracks.test.ts, neither of which exists yet. No task in any state declares either path. The active tasks are PW-0208 (REVIEW, apps/desktop/**), PW-0307 (IN_PROGRESS, eleven named apps/web and e2e files, none under components/player), PW-0602 (IN_PROGRESS, e2e/windows/** and the windows workflow) and PL-0714 (REVIEW, ci.yml). None of them names components/player in either field, and PW-0206 names none of theirs. PW-0306 holds components/player/controls/** and player-surface.tsx and is BACKLOG.

A DEPENDENCY CHANGE IS NOT A SURFACE CHANGE AND DOES NOT AFFECT ANY FINGERPRINT. requireAllDependenciesDone is what it moves: PW-0206 becomes dispatchable because PW-0202 is DONE.

PW-0206 allowedPaths += apps/web/src/components/player/player-adapter.ts, player-adapter.test.ts, web-player-adapter.ts, web-player-adapter.test.ts. Recorded BEFORE any file is written.

WHY, AND IT IS THE FIRST 'REQUIRED' CLAUSE RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. The acceptance asks for 'one normalised track vocabulary that BOTH adapters answer in' and for the DEFAULT selection to come from the policy already contracted in packages/contracts/src/domains/audio.ts and subtitles.ts 'rather than a second policy being invented here'. Those two clauses cannot both be satisfied inside tracks.ts alone, because the vocabulary PW-0201 shipped is LOSSY against exactly the fields that policy decides on, and the loss is concentrated in the accessibility fields:

  - audioTrackSchema needs  (main / original / dub / descriptive / commentary). PlayerTrack has no role field at all. The policy's AUTO_SELECTABLE_ROLES exists to keep commentary and audio-description OUT of automatic selection, so a bridge that defaulted the missing role to 'main' would hand a viewer a commentary track automatically -- the precise harm the contract was written to prevent.
  - subtitleTrackSchema needs  (subtitles / sdh / forced / commentary). PlayerTrack has only the boolean isForced, so sdh and commentary are not representable. subtitles.ts says SDH is 'frequently the ONLY subtitle track a title ships in a given language, so it must remain automatically selectable for everyone'; a vocabulary that cannot say 'sdh' cannot express that.
  - subtitleTrackSchema needs  (webvtt / ttml / srt / ass) and the policy rejects a format the client cannot render. PlayerTrack has a free-text  and no format.

THE INFORMATION IS NOT MISSING FROM THE ENGINE, ONLY FROM THE BOUNDARY. Shaka's text tracks carry roles, kind, forced and mimeType, and its variant tracks carry roles, audioRoles, audioCodec and channelsCount; web-player-adapter.ts's #readTracks reads a subset and drops the rest. So the fix is to widen the boundary and have the adapter answer, which is what 'both adapters answer in' means, rather than to invent the fields in a bridge or to start a second vocabulary beside the first.

THE ALTERNATIVE WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: tracks.ts could declare its own richer track type and have adapters supply it through a side channel. That is two vocabularies for one thing, which is what the clause forbids, and it is how the UI ends up branching on engine.

SCOPE, HELD DELIBERATELY NARROW. Four named files, not components/player/**. The change to the adapter is ADDITIVE -- new fields, each nullable, each null meaning 'the engine did not state it' and never a guess. Nothing existing is removed or renamed. PW-0205 and PW-0306 are unaffected in their own surfaces and must answer in the widened vocabulary when they land, which is the direction a contract is supposed to travel.

CONFLICT-CHECKED IN BOTH FIELDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. player-adapter.ts and its test belong to PW-0201 (DONE); web-player-adapter.ts and its test to PW-0202 (DONE). No other task in any state declares any of the four in either field -- grep over the whole board. The active tasks are PW-0208 (REVIEW, apps/desktop/**), PW-0307 (IN_PROGRESS, eleven named files, none under components/player), PW-0602 (IN_PROGRESS, e2e/windows/** and windows.yml) and PL-0714 (REVIEW, ci.yml). PW-0306 (BACKLOG) holds components/player/controls/** and player-surface.tsx, neither of which is taken here. Only two files in the repository reference PlayerTrack and both are now on this surface, so the widening cannot break a caller that is out of reach.

A FINGERPRINT CONSEQUENCE, STATED: widening allowedPaths widens what an approval of PW-0206 fingerprints. That is correct -- these files are part of the reviewed change -- and it is recorded so the review range is not a surprise.

CORRECTION to the immediately preceding task.definition_changed event (PW-0206 allowedPaths). THAT EVENT IS DAMAGED AND THE DAMAGE IS MINE. It was typed into a double-quoted shell string containing backticked identifiers, so the shell performed command substitution on them and the words were replaced by nothing. The three sentences that lost a word read "audioTrackSchema needs  (main / original / dub / descriptive / commentary)", "subtitleTrackSchema needs  (subtitles / sdh / forced / commentary)" and "subtitleTrackSchema needs  (webvtt / ttml / srt / ass)" and "a free-text  and no format". THE MISSING WORDS ARE, IN ORDER: role, kind, format, codec.

The event log is append-only, so the damaged entry stays and this corrects it rather than replacing it. The task notes written in the same operation were produced by a quoted heredoc and are undamaged; so are every other event, gate result and commit message of this round, which were checked by scanning for the collapsed-whitespace signature that command substitution leaves. Only that one entry is affected and only in those four places.

Recorded as an operator error rather than quietly re-stating the facts in the next event, because the audit trail is the thing it is for.

evidence: npm run typecheck: 22 tasks successful, 22 total. npm run lint: 12 tasks successful, 0 errors; the single warning is a pre-existing unused import in apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.test.ts, which is not on this surface and was not introduced here. npm run test: 22 tasks successful, 22 total. apps/web 85 files / 1534 tests, up from 84 / 1494 -- 40 new tests, 0 failed, nothing else disturbed. Whole repository green: provider-sdk 288, catalog-ingestion 152, backend 36, media-engine and the rest unchanged.

NEW COVERAGE, 40 CASES IN TWO FILES.
tracks.test.ts, 31 cases: codec normalisation including the RFC 6381 spellings a manifest actually states and a null for everything unrecognised; conversion with and without each assumption; the refusal to convert a sub-minimum language tag, which the contract declares .min(2) and which would otherwise build an object the schema rejects; identity and the four re-application confidences; and the resolution, including the clause this task exists for.
web-player-adapter.test.ts, 9 new cases over the three fields the adapter now reads.

THE SUITE WAS MUTATION-TESTED RATHER THAN TRUSTED, because 31 cases passing on the first run is a reason to check the tests, not to celebrate. Four mutations, each reverted:
  1. short-circuit a viewer "off" to null instead of passing the mode to the policy -> 2 failed. This is the one that matters: the contract records that a FORCED track survives an off preference, and the short circuit is the plausible implementation that deletes the only subtitle a non-reading viewer needs.
  2. let reapply match two tracks that both state no language -> 1 failed.
  3. tell the subtitle policy nothing about the audio that will actually play -> 2 failed. A forced track is keyed to the soundtrack, so this is what makes audio-before-subtitle load-bearing rather than tidy.
  4. drop the assumptions from the result -> 1 failed.
All four caught; restored, 31 passed.

THE RE-APPLICATION CLAUSE IS TESTED AS THE REAL EVENT. A candidate switch that renames EVERY id (cdn2/ prefix on all four tracks) still restores the viewer French audio and French subtitles, because a choice is remembered as a language and a purpose rather than as a track id -- WebPlayerAdapter builds audio ids as audio:<language> and takes subtitle ids from the manifest, so the ids genuinely do not survive the teardown the clause names.

ORDER-INVARIANCE IS A PROPERTY TEST, not an example: fast-check over 60 shuffles of a four-track list, asserting the same audio and subtitle answer every time. The policy claims order-invariance and this module must not reintroduce a dependency on the way in.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No browser ran any of this, no real Shaka instance produced a track list, and no mpv adapter exists to confirm it can answer in this vocabulary -- that is PW-0205 and it is sequenced after. The Shaka field names the adapter reads (audioRoles, roles, kind, mimeType, forced, channelsCount, audioCodec) are read from a fake player in the suite, as every other test in that file does; they are not verified against a running Shaka.

message:
PL-0716 created by the round-107 project-wide gap hunt. control/product-readiness.json -- the instrument that answers "can a person install this and watch something", deliberately separate from the task count -- has gone stale in the direction that makes the product look WORSE than it is, and it is the figure the commander reads.

Nine demonstrably false items, each checkable in one command. The two that matter most: packagingRelease.windows-build says "Every CI job is ubuntu-latest; no windows-latest runner exists" and cites three ci.yml line numbers, while windows.yml and desktop-shell-ci.yml both run on windows-latest and both SUCCEEDED on 2c037d5; packagingRelease.installer says "No NSIS, WiX, MSI, MSIX or Inno configuration anywhere" while the Windows job produces one MSI and one NSIS installer every run, digests them, installs the MSI, verifies the installed tree and uninstalls it. That dimension reports 0 percent. Also stale: app-identity, tauri-shell, capability-routing, track-selection, offline-network-state (PW-0309 shipped all three things it says are missing), windows-e2e (25 Rust tests run on windows-latest every push), and several notes describing PW-0102, PW-0303, PW-0312 and PW-0403 as in REVIEW when all are DONE.

THE TASK DOES NOT LICENSE OPTIMISM. Its acceptance requires the file own scoring rules to be APPLIED rather than relaxed -- present still means reachable by a user of the shipped app, so an installer nobody has launched moves to partial and not to present -- and requires each correction to state WHICH KIND it is, because a figure that rises because the product improved and one that rises because the instrument was wrong are different events. The rules, weights and dimension list are explicitly out of scope.

ONE ITEM IS TO BE MADE MORE PRECISE RATHER THAN FLIPPED: engineeringFoundation.rate-limits, "No rate limit on any route", is false for the auth routes and true for the application own routes. better-auth 1.7.5 enables rate limiting whenever the server is in production and applies three requests per ten seconds to anything under /sign-in and /sign-up. That is not pedantry: PL-0715, this round new e2e failure, is very likely a consequence of the half that exists.

NOBODY OWNED THE FILE -- control/** and coordination/** belong to PL-0002, PL-AI-0001 and PL-AI-0002, all DONE. Same shape as the windows.yml gap reported in round 105 and closed in round 107. Lane Coordination, which is PL-AI-0002 own lane and the lane a status instrument belongs to. Conflict-checked in both fields in both directions: no task in any state names either path, and none of the five active tasks touches them.

scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs CAN BLOCK FOR TENS OF MINUTES INSIDE unlink(), AND THAT WAS OBSERVED RATHER THAN INFERRED.

WHAT WAS DONE. npm run test:scripts was started in this container at 17:11 with NODE_OPTIONS=--report-on-fatalerror and WITHOUT the --max-old-space-size=8192 this container normally sets -- the confounder round 106 found in every earlier measurement of this suite. It was still running 75 minutes later.

WHAT THE PROCESS IS DOING, read from /proc rather than guessed.
  state Sl, 7 threads, RSS 108 MB -- not a memory problem by any reading.
  TOTAL CPU 12 SECONDS across 34 minutes of being the control-plane suite. It is not computing.
  /proc/<pid>/syscall begins 87, which is unlink.
  /proc/<pid>/wchan is submit_bio_wait -- blocked in block-layer I/O.
  Every other thread is in futex_do_wait or ep_poll; nothing else is doing anything.
  No child processes at all, so it is not waiting on a spawn.
  One /tmp/liberty-control-plane-* root remains, 1.5 GB, and it was not shrinking measurably.

WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES. The suite copies the working tree roughly 69 times and holds every copy -- filed as a defect in round 104 -- and its TEARDOWN is synchronous recursive deletion on the main thread. That deletion is unbounded in wall-clock time and is filesystem-bound, not CPU-bound and not heap-bound. Round 106 said of the CI abort: "an abort at 10m38 lands near the END of that suite rather than early -- possibly in its final rmSync. That is arithmetic, not evidence." It is now an observation. The suite genuinely does spend open-ended time in deletion.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, AND IS NOT CLAIMED. This is not a cause for CI exit 134. A process blocked in unlink does not raise SIGABRT; it hangs. The two may share a root -- a suite that writes and deletes gigabytes is the part of this job most exposed to a filesystem running out of room or out of patience -- or they may be unrelated. PL-0714 exists so the next CI occurrence produces evidence instead of a number, and nothing in it assumes this.

CONFOUNDERS, STATED. This run competed for two cores and one disk with a full npm run test, two typechecks, a lint and a vitest suite while PW-0206 was implemented. The container is at 77 percent disk with 9.8 GB free. A GitHub runner has four cores, more free disk and a different storage layer. So the DURATION here is not transferable. The BLOCKING SITE is, because it is a property of the code.

THE REMEDY IS NOT THIS ROUND'S. It belongs with the round-104 defect: do not hold 69 copies, and do not delete them synchronously on the main thread at the end. Filed here as an observation so whoever takes that work starts from a measurement.

CORRECTION, AND IT IS A CORRECTION OF MY OWN MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A NEW FINDING. The preceding defect.found event about scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs blocking in unlink() contains two errors and omits the thing that actually happened.

ERROR 1: IT SAYS THE SUITE WAS "STILL RUNNING 75 MINUTES LATER". It was not. It ran for 2090 seconds -- 34.8 minutes -- and then exited. The /proc readings quoted in that event were taken at 33 and 34 minutes elapsed, which is moments before the end, not an hour into a hang. The 75-minute figure was wall-clock since I started it and I wrote it as the process's elapsed time without checking; `ps -o etimes` said 2019, 2025 and 2051 in the very output I was reading from.

ERROR 2: IT OMITS THAT THE SUITE THEN FAILED, AND WHY. Exit 1, on the suite's own safety assertion: "running the test suite must not mutate the real control/tasks.json". THAT FAILURE IS MINE AND NOT THE SUITE'S. The run started at 17:11 and I went on editing control/tasks.json throughout it -- creating PL-0714, PL-0715 and PL-0716, amending PW-0206 twice. The suite snapshots the real tasks.json and refuses to finish if it changed, which is a good assertion doing exactly its job on an operator who mutated the repository under a test that copies the repository. It says nothing about the suite's health and nothing about CI, where the tree is a quiescent checkout.

WHAT SURVIVES, UNCHANGED. The blocking site is still a real measurement and is still a property of the code: at 34 minutes elapsed the process had used TWELVE SECONDS of CPU, state Sl, RSS 108 MB, no child processes, main-thread syscall 87 (unlink), wchan submit_bio_wait, every other thread in futex_do_wait or ep_poll. The suite's teardown is synchronous recursive deletion on the main thread and it is filesystem-bound. What the corrected timing changes is the WEIGHT: a teardown that takes minutes at the end of a 35-minute suite is a cost, not a hang, and I presented it as closer to a hang than the numbers support.

WHAT IS STILL NOT CLAIMED: any connection to CI exit 134. Less than before, if anything.

A CLEAN RE-RUN FOLLOWS, with the tree quiescent, so there is one measurement that is not confounded by its own observer.

A CLEAN, UNCONFOUNDED MEASUREMENT OF npm run test:scripts, which is what the validate job runs.

EXIT 0, 2229 SECONDS (37.2 minutes), tree quiescent throughout, NODE_OPTIONS=--report-on-fatalerror and WITHOUT this container's usual --max-old-space-size=8192. All six suites green:
  test-validate-env           38 scenarios
  test-ai-control-plane       73 scenarios
  test-validate-repo          20 assertion groups, plus workspace-deps 27 and turbo-graph 21 delegated from it
  test-desktop-target         9 assertions      <- newly wired into CI this round
  cloud/test-dispatcher       35 scenarios
  windows/test-lifecycle      30 pass, 0 fail   <- newly wired into CI this round
No /tmp/liberty-control-plane-* roots left behind; the teardown completed.

THE DURATION IS THE FINDING AND IT IS A TREND, NOT A VERDICT. Round 104 and round 106 measured this suite at 1261 s ambient and 1807 s under a runner-like 4 GB heap cap. It is now 2229 s on the same container with no cap and nothing else running. Why it should grow is visible while it runs: the suite spawns a FRESH node per scenario -- `node scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs <command>` at 100 percent CPU for seconds at a time -- and every one of them parses the whole of control/tasks.json, which is about 1.5 MB and has grown every round. The suite's runtime therefore scales with the size of the board, and the board only grows.

WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT SAY ABOUT CI EXIT 134. It does NOT explain it, and I am not offering it as an explanation: validate PASSED at 25m 4s and 27m 29s and then ABORTED at 10m 38s and 10m 26s. An abort at less than half the passing time is not a job that ran out of time, and a growth trend predicts the opposite of what was observed. What it does say is that this suite is on a trajectory toward whatever the job's practical ceiling turns out to be, independently of the current failure, and that the round-104 defect -- roughly 69 tree copies, all held, deleted synchronously at the end -- is the place to spend the next effort.

EARLIER TODAY THE SAME COMMAND EXITED 1 AT 2090 s, ON THE SUITE'S OWN ASSERTION THAT THE RUN MUST NOT MUTATE THE REAL control/tasks.json. That was mine: I edited tasks.json four times while it ran. This run is the clean one.

PW-0306 allowedPaths += apps/web/src/components/player/player-adapter.ts, player-adapter.test.ts, web-player-adapter.ts, web-player-adapter.test.ts. Recorded BEFORE any file is written.

WHY, AND IT IS AN ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. The acceptance requires "a seek bar with BUFFERED RANGES", "a subtitle menu and an audio-track menu driven by PW-0206", and -- the clause that decides this -- "the controls read THE ADAPTER, not Shaka, so the same UI operates the native engine". Two of those three are unreachable through PlayerAdapter as it stands.

1. THE ADAPTER CANNOT REPORT TRACKS UNLESS IT PERFORMED THE LOAD. WebPlayerAdapter populates its track list inside load() and nowhere else, so getTracks() answers an empty array forever in this application -- because player-surface.tsx does not load through the adapter. It loads through the machine's existing loadCandidate effect, which calls PlaybackController.setSource.

   ROUTING THE LOAD THROUGH THE ADAPTER WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED ON A RIGHTS GROUND, not a difficulty one. PlayerAdapter.load takes a PlayerSession whose candidates carry `protection` and `compatibility`. The client-side PlaybackSession in playback-session.ts carries neither -- it is {id, providerId, source}. Projecting one into the other would mean INVENTING a protection value and a compatibility confidence for a rights-bearing decision, which is the second opinion PW-0203 exists to prevent and which player-adapter.ts's own header refuses in writing. The wire contract already carries both fields; the client projection drops them. That reconciliation is PW-0203's by gpt-architect's round-82 ruling and is NOT taken here.

2. THE ADAPTER CANNOT REPORT BUFFERED RANGES AT ALL. The buffering event carries fillPercent, which is a number, not a set of ranges, and a seek bar needs the ranges.

WHAT IS BEING ADDED, AND WHY IT IS A BOUNDARY CONCEPT RATHER THAN A HOLE PUNCHED FOR A UI.
  resynchronise(): re-read state from the engine and publish it. This is already a first-class idea in this boundary: PlayerAdapterEvent has a `resynchronised` member, and PW-0204's acceptance requires the mpv event pump to handle MPV_EVENT_QUEUE_OVERFLOW "by resynchronising from properties rather than by assuming the queue is authoritative". The capability was specified and never given a method. Adding it is completing the boundary, not bending it, and mpv will need it for its own reasons.
  getBufferedRanges(): a pull-side read beside the three the interface already has (getTimeline, getTracks, readAvSyncTelemetry), returning the existing BufferedRange type from diagnostics/buffered-ranges.ts rather than a second two-field interface spelling the same thing. Type-only import, so nothing enters the runtime import graph the player-adapter guard walks.

THE ALTERNATIVE WAS REJECTED: player-surface.tsx could read Shaka's track list and the element's buffered ranges itself and pass them to the controls as data. That duplicates WebPlayerAdapter's own #readTracks in a second place -- the drift this repository has been bitten by three times -- and it means the same UI would have nothing to read on the native engine, which is the exact clause the acceptance writes in capitals.

CONFLICT-CHECKED IN BOTH FIELDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. All four files belonged to PW-0206, which is DONE as of this round, and before that to PW-0201 and PW-0202, both DONE. A CORRECTION THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE DEFECT IT CAME WITH: THE CI ANNOTATION HAS BEEN NAMING THE FAILING STEP ALL ALONG, AND TWO ROUNDS OF HANDOFFS SAID OTHERWISE.

WHAT WAS CLAIMED. Round 106: "the annotation names an exit code and no step, and the log needs authentication". Round 107 repeated it and built part of PL-0714 on it: "the annotation names no step ... the whole evidence available was a number".

WHAT IS TRUE. The RUN page does not show which step an annotation belongs to. The JOB page does, and it needs no authentication either. The job URL is on the run page as a link; nobody followed it.

THE FACT THAT WAS SITTING THERE. Run 37036128012, validate job 110934662749, read today: exit code 134 under the step "TEST AI CONTROL PLANE". That is the suite that has been the prime suspect since round 104 -- the one that copies the working tree roughly 69 times and holds every copy, and that was measured this week blocked in unlink() with twelve seconds of CPU in thirty-four minutes. The confirmation was available on the first day and was obtained by reading a different URL, not by any mechanism PL-0714 added.

CONSEQUENCES, STATED RATHER THAN SOFTENED.
1. PL-0714's step-outcome table was partly justified on a GitHub limitation that does not exist. The comment in .github/workflows/ci.yml that asserted it has been corrected IN THE FILE, where the next reader will meet it, rather than only here. What the table is still worth is narrower and is now written down: it distinguishes a step that FAILED from one that never STARTED, which an annotation cannot, and it survives a job killed without an annotation at all.
2. The machine-facts step and the redacted V8 report are untouched by this: neither was ever available from an annotation.
3. The standing research rule from here on: read the JOB page, not the run page. The run page is a summary and it drops the attribution.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It names the step; it does not explain the abort. "Test AI control plane" exiting 134 is consistent with the round-104 defect and is not proof of it, and CI #178 ran that same step to completion at 975331c, so it does not reproduce on demand either. No cause is claimed.

That is consistent with PL-0715's diagnosis -- a rate-limit window that several parallel workers sometimes exceed and sometimes do not -- and is NOT a reason to close PL-0715: an intermittent defect that passes once is an intermittent defect.

Production + real PostgreSQL 16, cold database, --workers=4: 77 passed / 46 skipped / 0 failed; the five skip there with their reason named, because /watch refuses before a player exists on a build with no catalog source.

HOW THE END OF PLAYBACK IS REACHED IN A BROWSER, AND EXACTLY WHAT IS SIMULATED. No real media decodes in this harness -- the demo catalog's sources are fixtures -- so nothing can play a programme to its end. What the test dispatches is the `ended` EVENT ON THE REAL <liberty-video> ELEMENT, which is the event a real ending fires. Everything downstream is the product and none of it is stubbed: WebPlayerAdapter's own listener, its `ended` adapter event, the machine's MEDIA_ENDED, the transition into the `ended` phase, and player-surface rendering from that phase. THE ONLY THING FAKED IS THE DECODER. It is dispatched rather than the `ended` property being assigned, because the element's listeners are what the adapter attached to and a property would prove nothing about the wiring.

THE FIVE CASES.
  NOTHING IS OFFERED UNTIL THE PROGRAMME ENDS -- and the prompt is asserted absent from the DOCUMENT, not merely invisible. A hidden affordance is still in the accessibility tree, and a screen reader that can find "Next episode" mid-programme has been told the ending early.
  When it ends, S1 E2 is offered AND ONLY OFFERED: the URL is still the episode the viewer was watching. Nothing counts down and nothing navigates.
  The offer is a LINK with the accessible name "Play S1 E2" -- not "Play", which is what a screen-reader user meets out of context -- it is focusable, Enter follows it, and it lands on /watch/<next>, the ORDINARY route with the ordinary session request and the ordinary authorization decision. No bespoke play-next path.
  AT THE END OF THE SERIES, NOTHING IS OFFERED AND NOTHING WRAPS AROUND. A player that wrapped to S1 E1 would fail the deterministic-end clause in the most confusing possible way.
  A FILM OFFERS NOTHING, because "next" is a question about a series.

MUTATION-TESTED IN THE BROWSER, NOT ONLY IN UNIT TESTS. Rendering the prompt regardless of the machine phase: 1 failed. Dropping nextUp on the watch page: 2 failed. Both reverted.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The ending was dispatched, not decoded. The rights gate's refusal path at this affordance -- an episode whose basis lapses between the page render and the click -- is not exercised here and cannot be: the gate runs on the server at render time, and /watch/:id re-decides on arrival, which is the arrangement that makes the stale case safe rather than a case this spec can stage.

A tab-order trace of the same page showed the browser reaching every one of them, so the gate was wrong, not the product, and both causes were defects in the gate. First, identity was the human-readable description, and a title page renders one Play link per episode row that all describe as a.episodePlay "Play"; the walk stops when focus returns to something already visited, so the second identical description read as a wrap-around, the walk ended after two rows, and three real reachable links were reported as defects. Second, the gate judged a page that had not finished arriving: SeasonNavigation renders every season panel open on the server and hides the unselected ones only once it knows it has hydrated, so season 2's links were observed while visible and walked once they were not. The spec now waits for the DOM to stop changing before observing. A unit test was added for the collision: two elements with the same description and different probes, one reached and one not.

The remaining REQUIRED clauses are therefore about COST and about FOCUS, not about reachability: a rail of five cards is up to fifteen tab stops because every card carries a heading link, a My List control and sometimes a Start over link, and the home page is two or three such rails.

PL-0719 SURFACE AMENDMENT, recorded before any write, and it begins with a correction. The allowedPaths this task was FILED with -- apps/web/src/lib/auth/** and apps/web/src/lib/auth-policy.ts -- DO NOT EXIST. They were guessed while filing the task from another lane, on the strength of a component file named apps/web/src/components/auth/auth-policy.ts, and neither was checked against the tree. That is a declaration that would have reserved nothing and enforced nothing, and it is being replaced rather than quietly widened.

WHERE THE POLICY ACTUALLY LIVES, read from the code. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts is the ONLY module in the repository that imports better-auth, by design, and its option object has NO rateLimit key at all -- which is exactly why the product inherits the library's default. packages/auth/src/config.ts is the validated schema every environment value passes through. packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts already holds the mechanism this task needs: ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES as an allowlist, describeConfiguredSurface as a HAND-WRITTEN second reading of the option object, and findSurfaceViolations comparing the two, with the file's own comment explaining that a report derived from the allowlist would agree with it by construction and be decoration. A rate-limit policy that is stated in this repository is a capability in that allowlist and a line in that report. apps/web/src/lib/session/auth-instance.ts is the composition root that builds the config from LIBERTY_AUTH_* variables and calls assertSurfaceIsMinimal.

PATHS NOW: packages/auth/src/rate-limit.ts and packages/auth/src/rate-limit.test.ts (new, the policy and its reasoning); packages/auth/src/config.ts and config.test.ts; packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts; packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts and enabled-surface.test.ts; packages/auth/src/index.ts; apps/web/src/lib/session/auth-instance.ts and auth-instance.test.ts; e2e/tests/auth-rate-limit.spec.ts (new). The e2e file is here because the acceptance REQUIRES a test that tells a rate-limited refusal apart from a wrong-credential one, and that distinction only exists against a real server: throttling is enabled on a production build and off in development, which is the divergence the task exists to make deliberate.

REVIEW DEPENDENCIES: e2e/src/identity.ts, which is where PL-0715 taught the harness to tell the two refusals apart and is the evidence the gap is real; docs/RESEARCH_IDENTITY.md, which is the ruling the enabled surface implements; apps/web/src/app/api/auth; docs/API_CONTRACTS.md. None of them is reserved.

CONFLICT-CHECKED IN BOTH FIELDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS at amendment. Active tasks are PL-0714 (.github/workflows/ci.yml), PW-0208 (apps/desktop/**, docs/LICENSING.md), PW-0307 (sixteen named apps/web and e2e files), PW-0310 (apps/web/src/lib/a11y/**, app/globals.css, app/layout.tsx, four rail containers, two test files, e2e/tests/keyboard-reachability.spec.ts) and PW-0602 (e2e/windows/**, .github/workflows/windows.yml). NO ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE IS WEAKENED by this amendment. The prohibitions stand unchanged: the control may not be weakened, no bypass of any kind may be added, and CAPTCHA, lockout and fingerprinting stay out of scope.
