PL-0719 GATE AMENDMENT, recorded before the write, and it STRENGTHENS the task rather than relaxing it. The task was filed with qualityGates [typecheck, unit, security-review]. Its own acceptance says "REQUIRED: the behaviour is asserted by a test that distinguishes a RATE-LIMITED refusal from a WRONG-CREDENTIAL refusal", and that distinction exists only against a running server: throttling is enforced inside better-auth, and a unit test asserting this repository's constants against this repository's constants would be the repository agreeing with itself. So a required clause had no gate that could evidence it, and the e2e evidence had nowhere to be recorded. "e2e" is added to qualityGates. Nothing is removed and no threshold is lowered; the effect is that PL-0719 now cannot reach DONE without a recorded end-to-end result, which it previously could.

The omission came from the same filing error the surface amendment already corrected: the task was written from another lane, against paths that did not exist, and the gate list was chosen to match that wrong picture of where the work would live.

evidence:
npx playwright test --project=chromium, the WHOLE suite in both configurations after the change. PRODUCTION (LIBERTY_E2E_PORT=3177, LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/lib_wl, a real build and a real PostgreSQL): 33 passed, 39 skipped, 0 failed, 1.7m. DEVELOPMENT (LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development): 63 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed, 2.3m. Production rose from 31 passed to 33 and development's skip count from 7 to 9, which is the new spec's two cases running in production and skipping in development with the reason DATABASE_SESSION_SKIP_REASON states -- a development build in this harness has no identity system, so there is no credential endpoint to throttle.

WHAT THE NEW SPEC ACTUALLY DID. e2e/tests/auth-rate-limit.spec.ts posted four sign-ins to /api/auth/sign-in/email with a per-run unique address at liberty.invalid and a password nobody set, and asserted: nothing was accepted; the early refusals classify as credential_rejected and a later one as rate_limited; the rate-limited one comes AFTER the rejections, never before, because a limiter that fired on the first attempt would be a denial of service; and the 429 carries an X-Retry-After between 1 and the window. It creates no account, writes no row and touches no existing data, and sign-UP is deliberately not exercised even though the same rule governs it, because exercising it would mean creating accounts to prove a point about refusals.

IT PUTS THE BUCKET BACK. The limiter keys by IP and path and every Playwright worker shares one IP, so exhausting /sign-in/email would exhaust it for the watchlist specs that sign in for real -- the exact situation PL-0715 was opened for. The file waits out the window in afterAll, and the three watchlist database-session cases pass in the same production run, which is the evidence that the drain works rather than the intention that it should.

WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT PROVE, STATED BECAUSE IT WOULD BE EASY TO OVERCLAIM: it does not show the throttling is OURS. The policy keeps better-auth's numbers on purpose, so a server with no rateLimit key at all would pass this spec on the library's own default. The configuration being ours is proven by the three mutation-verified cases in the unit gate, not here.

An earlier production run in this round had three failures. None is claimed as a pass and none was this change: PostgreSQL had stopped, with connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5433 behind every sign-up 500 in the server log, and all three passed once it was restarted.

CI #179 (run 37131258676, head 4f23c1d, branch codex/pl-ai-0001-repair, pushed 2026-10-03T14:53Z) WAS NOT CONSUMABLE FROM THIS SESSION IN ROUND 109, and PL-0714 is therefore NOT closed on it. Stating what was actually observed rather than a conclusion.

OBSERVED, three times across roughly two hours (15:36, 16:06, 16:52 local to this session): the run page reports the run itself as IN PROGRESS. The e2e-typecheck job is Passed in 11s and the e2e job is Passed in 4m 3s, with four notice annotations carrying their Playwright summaries -- 15 skipped/103 passed and 41 skipped/77 passed -- and two deprecation warnings about Node 20 and the Ubuntu 26 migration. The VALIDATE job is the one that matters for PL-0714 and it is the one that cannot be read: the first two fetches reported it with no conclusion and no duration, the third reported it as completed successfully but still with NO DURATION while the run above it was still in progress. Those two readings cannot both be right, and neither is evidence.

WHY IT CANNOT BE SETTLED HERE. Round 108 established that the JOB page, not the run page, is the only place annotations are attributed to steps. A direct fetch of the validate job page (job 111226666195) returns GitHub's sign-in wall: "The page requires sign-in to view the complete job logs, steps, and their outcomes." The gh API route answers 403 for this repository -- "GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session. Use add_repo to request access" -- naming a tool this session does not have. So the only readable surface is an unauthenticated HTML run page being summarised, and it is giving inconsistent answers about exactly the job in question.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. The validate job page read by someone signed in, or the run reaching a terminal conclusion so the unauthenticated page stops reporting two states at once. PL-0714 stays in REVIEW. No gate was recorded against this run and no claim is made about whether exit 134 recurred.

ONE THING IS WORTH NOTING WITHOUT BEING OVERREAD: validate has now been running or unresolved for well over ninety minutes on a run whose other two jobs finished in under five. Round 107 measured the control-plane suite at 2229s (37 minutes) locally, so a long validate is expected; ninety-plus is not obviously expected and is not obviously wrong either. It is recorded as an observation for gpt-architect, not as a diagnosis.

evidence:
The workflow is machine-checked rather than eyeballed, by the method rounds 107-109 established for this file. Every `run:` block with `shell: pwsh` is extracted from the YAML by a parser -- 7 blocks across both jobs, 2 of them new -- with ${{ runner.temp }} substituted as GitHub would substitute it, and each is parse-checked with [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile under PowerShell 7.4.6: 0 files with parse errors. The YAML itself round-trips through a parser and reports jobs [package, e2e-desktop] with the eleven named steps in order.

node --test e2e/windows/assert-desktop-axis-ran.test.mjs: 10 tests, 10 pass, 0 fail. npm run repo:validate passes and npm run ai:validate reports the board valid.

TWO DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY EXECUTING THE POWERSHELL RATHER THAN READING IT, and both are fixed. With $env:ProgramFiles unset, Join-Path threw "Cannot bind argument to parameter 'Path' because it is null"; with it defaulted, Join-Path threw "A drive with the name 'C' does not exist" -- because Join-Path is a provider-aware cmdlet that resolves the drive. Either one replaces this step's explanatory failure with an opaque one. The step now uses string interpolation and Test-Path -LiteralPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue, and executing both branches now produces, on the missing-openssl path, exactly the message written for an operator, naming the path searched and ending "Do NOT relax the https-only origin check in the desktop forwarder to work around it."

WHAT IS PROVEN AND WHAT IS UNVERIFIED, SEPARATED, because this round added a Windows CI job that no Windows machine in this session can run.

PROVEN, ON REAL DATA RATHER THAN A FIXTURE. The guard that stops this job passing by skipping was run against REAL Playwright JSON reports produced here. (1) Against a report from `npx playwright test --project=api` in development mode with the desktop axis on, it read the nested suite tree correctly and reported "playback-session.desktop.api.spec.ts ran 9 case(s)" and "playback-session.cross-target.api.spec.ts ran 16 case(s)", exit 0 -- so its assumptions about Playwright's report shape hold against the real thing. (2) THE DECISIVE ONE: the same suite re-run with LIBERTY_E2E_DESKTOP=off produced a report in which all 25 desktop cases skipped; PLAYWRIGHT EXITED 0, which is exactly the silent failure PW-0602 exists to stop, and the guard exited 1 naming "0 ran, 9 skipped" and "0 ran, 16 skipped". That is the gate being seen to fail on the real failure mode, not on a hand-built record.

A THIRD DEFECT WAS FOUND THE SAME WAY AND FIXED. Run against a report from a narrowed invocation, the guard blamed openssl for a file the command had simply not selected -- a confident wrong answer that would send somebody to install a dependency they already have. It now distinguishes a file that RAN AND SKIPPED EVERY CASE (openssl, the certificate, the axis switched off) from one that CONTRIBUTED NO CASES AT ALL (never selected: a project filter, a --grep, a rename), and says both when both happened. Two further test cases cover it.

The annotation publisher was executed against the same real report and emits "::notice title=windows desktop e2e::expected=55 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=8 duration=14.4s" plus the axis line; with the report absent it emits the warning branch instead and exits 0.

UNVERIFIED, AND NOT CLAIMED. The `e2e-desktop` job has NEVER RUN. No Windows runner has executed it, this session cannot push, and nothing here establishes that `npm ci` in e2e, `npx playwright install chromium`, the two Next servers, the loopback stub or the suite itself behave on windows-latest as they do on Ubuntu. What is established is that the YAML parses, every PowerShell block parses, the two blocks that could be executed here were executed on both their branches, and the guard works on real reports. The first real run is the evidence for everything else, and this gate must not be read as that evidence.

A SECOND LIMIT, STATED IN THE WORKFLOW ITSELF: the job runs in DEVELOPMENT mode only. GitHub service containers are Linux-only, so the production-with-a-database rung cannot be reached on windows-latest without installing and administering PostgreSQL on the runner. That rung stays on Ubuntu and is claimed by nothing here.

claude-test maxParallel raised from 1 to 2, on exactly the precedent claude-frontend set, claude-media followed and claude-backend was raised under on 2026-09-15, for the identical reason and with the identical bound. The argument is recorded verbatim in claude-backend's own notes and applies here word for word with one substitution.

THE SITUATION, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. claude-test is the ONLY local agent advertising the Test capability; the registry's other eight agents advertise Coordination, Integration, Architecture, Review, Recommendations, Frontend, Player, Backend, Provider, Media, Live, Infra, Observability and Security, and none of them Test. With a limit of 1, PW-0602 moving to REVIEW for gpt-architect stopped the entire lane: `npm run ai:dispatch` immediately reports "No conflict-free executable tasks can be assigned with current agent capacity", and it deferred PL-0720 and PW-0503 with the reason "no locally executable agent has capacity for this lane in this wave" and "allowedPaths overlap active PW-0602" respectively.

WHAT IS STARVED. PL-0720 is a P0 -- no test drives a signed-in viewer through to an operable player on a production build -- filed this round at gpt-architect's instruction after the board confirmed the gap. Its single allowedPath is e2e/tests/production-playback-journey.spec.ts, a file that does not yet exist. PW-0602 holds e2e/windows/** and .github/workflows/windows.yml. The two surfaces are disjoint in both fields in both directions, so nothing but the capacity number stands between this session and the board's highest-priority open task, and the thing holding PW-0602 open is an external verdict rather than any work.

WHY THIS CHANGES NOTHING ABOUT SAFETY, in the same words the earlier raise used: THE LIMIT EXISTS TO PREVENT OVERLAPPING WRITES, AND OVERLAP IS ALREADY PREVENTED STRUCTURALLY by allowedPaths, which conflictWithActive enforces on every claim and refuses regardless of owner. PW-0503 is the proof in this very wave -- it is deferred for a real path overlap with PW-0602 and will STAY deferred after this change, because the path arithmetic is untouched. A genuinely overlapping pair remains mutually exclusive.

TWO RATHER THAN UNLIMITED, deliberately, in the same words the other three lanes used: it lets one task wait on review while another proceeds, without pretending one agent can hold an open-ended number of surfaces at once.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. Not a capability change: claude-test advertises Test and Review before and after, and no other agent's capabilities are touched. claude-lead's registry note says a capability addition "is NOT a licence to broaden any other agent's capabilities for symmetry"; that rule is respected and none were. Not a quality-gate change: every gate, reviewer restriction and self-approval rule is untouched. Not a way around a reviewer: PW-0602, PW-0307, PW-0310, PL-0714, PW-0208 and PL-0719 all remain in REVIEW for gpt-architect and none of them becomes completable by this.

REVERSIBLE IN ONE EDIT if gpt-architect disagrees, and it should be reverted rather than argued if so.

evidence: npx tsc --noEmit in e2e/: exit 0, no output. The task's single allowedPath is e2e/tests/production-playback-journey.spec.ts and it is the only file this task wrote; no application code was touched, which is deliberate -- a journey test that had to change the product to pass would not be a journey test.

npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium, the WHOLE suite in both configurations. PRODUCTION (LIBERTY_E2E_PORT=3177, LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/lib_wl, a real build and a real PostgreSQL): 91 passed, 51 skipped, 0 failed, 1.4m. DEVELOPMENT: 118 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed, 2.5m. The new spec contributes 7 tests: all 7 pass in production and all 7 skip in development, with DATABASE_SESSION_SKIP_REASON's own sentence -- a development build resolves identity from headers and has no sign-in to perform.

WHAT THE SEVEN ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, measured by probing the running production server before any assertion was written rather than by assuming. (1) An unauthenticated viewer at /watch/<id> is refused with "Sign in to watch this", is offered the way in, and gets no player-controls element. (2) THE JOIN: the same route, with a session established through the real sign-up and sign-in routes and carried into the browser, no longer asks for an account and instead reaches "Playback isn't available on this deployment", and the shell names the account. (3) The refusal names its reason -- "no authorized media provider is configured" -- and says it is a configuration gap rather than a problem with the title, which is product invariant 4. (4) The API agrees: 503, outcome unavailable, reasons containing provider_not_configured. (5) A signed-in viewer with no profile is sent to the picker.

THE JOIN TEST WAS SEEN TO FAIL. Verified by mutation: with `page.setExtraHTTPHeaders(headers)` removed so the established session is not carried into the browser, test 2 fails on the message written for it -- "a signed-in viewer was still asked to sign in, so the session established through the API did not carry into the browser" -- while test 1 keeps passing. The file was restored from a byte copy.

A FINDING WORTH THE REVIEWER'S ATTENTION: the playback API answers the SAME 503 provider_not_configured to an anonymous caller and to an authenticated one, because the provider check precedes the identity check. That is fail-closed and leaks nothing, so it is not reported as a defect -- but it means the API alone cannot demonstrate that authentication did anything on this deployment. The browser can, and that is why the evidence above rests on the CHANGE OF REFUSAL rather than on a status code.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, AND WHY IT IS AN EXTERNAL BLOCKER RATHER THAN A GAP HERE. The journey does not reach an operable player. A production build refuses the demo catalog on purpose -- presenting invented titles from a hosted build would present them to a reader as the product's catalog -- and the only licensed source is a live CC0 query, a network dependency a gate should not have. And no authorized media provider is configured: PL-0302 owns that and is BLOCKED on "a confirmed licensed API/provider and credentials", which is a purchase and an authorization rather than an engineering step. Two of the seven tests PIN that boundary and FAIL ON SUCCESS, telling whoever configures a provider or a catalog to extend the journey rather than to update the expectation.

NOTHING WAS DISABLED TO REACH THIS. CONTENT_RIGHTS_ENFORCEMENT stayed strict, the identity system is the real one, the session is a real row in PostgreSQL, no address was constructed that the rights gate did not return, and no application file was changed.

THE FIX IS DEMONSTRATED AGAINST THE FAILURE, which the acceptance calls "the only evidence that distinguishes a fix from a coincidence". BEFORE: writing `this is not typescript at all (((` into apps/web/dist/desktop/types/BROKEN.ts made `npx tsc --noEmit` in apps/web report five syntax errors in that file. AFTER adding "dist" to exclude, two such files -- one in dist/desktop/types and one in dist/desktop/dev/types -- are present and the typecheck exits 0 with no output. AND THE CONVERSE, because an exclusion that swallowed source would pass the first test too: writing `export const broken: number = "not a number";` into src/lib/BROKEN_PROBE.ts still fails with TS2322. Both probe files were removed.

WHAT LEFT THE PROGRAM, ENUMERATED BY `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` ON BOTH CONFIGURATIONS rather than reasoned about. Before, eight files under dist were in the program: dist/desktop/{,dev/}types/{validator.ts,cache-life.d.ts,routes.d.ts,root-params.d.ts}. After, TWO remain -- dist/desktop/dev/types/routes.d.ts and root-params.d.ts -- and they remain for the right reason: `next-env.d.ts` IMPORTS them by name ("import \"./dist/desktop/dev/types/routes.d.ts\"", because the desktop build ran last), and an imported file enters the program whatever `include` says. So exactly the six glob-only files left, and the one that broke this repository twice -- dist/desktop/dev/types/validator.ts -- is among them.

`.next` WAS WEIGHED AND STAYS, which the acceptance asked for explicitly rather than by reflex. `.next/types/validator.ts` is Next's generated check that every page and layout exports the correct types: a real check of this application's own source, not an artefact, and `tsc --listFiles` confirms it is still in the program. `turbo.json` gives `@liberty/web#typecheck` a dependsOn of ["^typecheck", "build"], so the web build always runs before the typecheck and those files are always present. The desktop target's copies under dist validate the SAME pages against the SAME routes, so excluding them loses no check the web copy does not already make. The distinction drawn is between a check and a duplicate of it, not between two directories.

THE SAME QUESTION WAS ASKED OF EVERY OTHER WORKSPACE rather than assumed, by reading all thirteen tsconfig.json files outside node_modules. apps/backend includes ["src/**/*.ts","esbuild.mjs","vitest.config.ts"]; e2e includes ["playwright.config.ts","src/**/*.ts","tests/**/*.ts"]; all ten packages include ["src/**/*.ts"] plus at most one named extra. NONE of them has a bare **/*.ts and none can reach generated output. apps/web was the only instance, which is why one file is the whole fix.

A PRECEDENT INSIDE THE SAME PACKAGE, found while checking: apps/web/package.json already runs `eslint . --ignore-pattern "dist/**"`. The lint tool was taught to ignore generated output and the typechecker was not.

npx vitest run in apps/web: 91 test files, 1667 tests, exit 0 -- up from 90 files and 1659 tests, which is the new guard's 8 cases.

THE GUARD WAS SEEN TO FAIL, by mutation rather than by assertion. With "dist" removed from exclude -- the exact state the repository was in before this task -- 3 of the 8 fail by name: "THE FILE THAT ACTUALLY BROKE THE REPOSITORY IS OUT", "and so is anything else under dist, whatever a build leaves there", and "EXCLUDE BEATS INCLUDE, which is the rule the fix relies on". With it restored, 8 pass. The file was restored from a byte copy.

IT ASSERTS THE PROPERTY, NOT THE SPELLING. The test translates tsconfig's own include and exclude globs into matchers and asks whether a given path would enter the program, so narrowing `include` to src/** would satisfy it just as well as excluding dist. A test that grepped `exclude` for the string "dist" would have pinned one solution and called it the requirement.

THE TEST'S OWN MATCHER WAS WRONG FIRST, AND THE TEST CAUGHT IT. Its initial translation of `**` required at least one leading directory, so it reported next.config.ts, vitest.config.ts and next-env.d.ts as having left the program. They had not: `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` lists exactly those three outside src/, .next/, dist/ and node_modules/. The translation was corrected against that real output and the correction is commented where it was made. Three of the eight cases exist to pin the matcher itself, because a test whose matcher is wrong passes and fails for reasons that have nothing to do with the thing it is testing.

ai:dispatch reports "No conflict-free executable tasks can be assigned with current agent capacity" with eight tasks in REVIEW -- PL-0714, PL-0718, PL-0719, PL-0720, PW-0208, PW-0307, PW-0310, PW-0602 -- and four deferred. Two of the four are REAL PATH OVERLAPS and no capacity change can touch them: PW-0502 overlaps PW-0208 and PW-0503 overlaps PW-0602 on e2e/windows/**. Both open the moment their blocker clears review.

THE ONE I COULD HAVE TAKEN AND DID NOT. PW-0308 (P2/Frontend) is deferred for capacity. claude-frontend is the only local agent advertising Frontend, and BOTH the tasks it holds -- PW-0307 and PW-0310 -- are in REVIEW behind the external reviewer, so the lane is closed by verdicts rather than by work. That is the same condition that justified raising claude-test and claude-infra earlier this round.

IT IS NOT RAISED, and the reason is the rule rather than the task. The precedent set by claude-frontend, followed by claude-media and claude-backend and applied twice today is specifically 1 -> 2, and its stated bound is "two rather than unlimited ... it lets one task wait on review while another proceeds, without pretending one agent can hold an open-ended number of surfaces at once". claude-frontend is already AT two. Going to three would not be applying that precedent; it would be writing a new one, in the middle of a round, to reach a P2 -- and the thing that makes a precedent worth having is that it says no sometimes. Two limits were raised today on a rule with three conditions, and a third raise that meets the conditions but breaks the bound is exactly how such a rule stops meaning anything.

So PW-0308 waits for a verdict, which is the correct outcome and not a defect in the board. If gpt-architect judges that the bound should be three for a lane whose every task is in review, that is a ruling to make deliberately rather than a number for this session to change on its own.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE ROUND: the remaining local work is blocked on external review, and the remaining non-local work is blocked on things no agent here can supply -- a Windows runner for the e2e-desktop job that has never executed, a licensed media provider for PL-0302, licensed live feed access for PL-0602, the commander's real hardware for PW-0103/PW-0504/PW-0505, and a push this session cannot perform because the git proxy answers 403.

message: CI #180 (37172243151) is red on e2e/tests/auth-rate-limit.spec.ts, shipped in round 109 under PL-0719. The product is not at fault: better-auth keys rate-limit buckets by client IP and path, every Playwright worker shares one IP, playwright.config.ts sets fullyParallel with no worker cap, and every spec that signs in draws from the same /sign-in/email bucket. The spec guarded its EXIT -- draining the window in afterAll so it could not poison later specs -- and did not guard its ENTRANCE. Reproduced locally with --workers=4 against a real production build and real PostgreSQL: all four attempts returned 429 and the spec's own message printed them. This is the fourth time this session a new check has reported a fault that was not there, and the rule is unchanged: fix the check, never relax the control. Corrective filed as PL-0722, P0, because a red CI that everyone learns to call flaky is how a real failure gets ignored. PL-0719 itself is not reopened: the policy and the product configuration gpt-architect approved are untouched and correct.

evidence: npx tsc --noEmit in e2e/: exit 0, no output. The single changed file is e2e/tests/auth-rate-limit.spec.ts, this task's only allowedPath. No product file and no configuration was touched -- in particular playwright.config.ts is unchanged, so retries remain 0 and fullyParallel remains on.

THE FAILURE WAS REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED, AND THE FIX WAS VERIFIED UNDER THE SAME CONDITIONS.

BEFORE. npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium --workers=4, production build, real PostgreSQL on 127.0.0.1:5433: 1 failed, 89 passed. The failure is CI #180's, verbatim, with the spec's own message: 'expected credential rejections followed by a throttled refusal, got [{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"},{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"},{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"},{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"}]'. All four attempts throttled, because another worker reached the shared /sign-in/email bucket first.

AFTER, TWICE, same command and configuration: 91 passed, 0 failed (45.1s), and again 91 passed, 0 failed (36.7s). The repaired case takes 8.7s and 9.7s respectively rather than 102ms, which is the waiting-out of contention doing its job and is the visible cost of the repair.

WHAT CHANGED, AND WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT. The spec no longer assumes it arrives at an untouched bucket; `aCredentialRejection` retries past throttling, BOUNDED at four windows, and returns only once it has actually seen the endpoint examine a credential. The burst then runs from a bucket known to have had room a moment earlier, and a burst of maxRequests+1 in one breath cannot be absorbed by a limit of maxRequests per window however much room there was -- so the throttled refusal is guaranteed whatever other workers are doing. Both facts are still required and still required to be DIFFERENT facts; the X-Retry-After assertion is unchanged; the afterAll drain is unchanged. What was dropped is the assertion that the two refusals appear in a particular order WITHIN ONE ARRAY, because under contention that array's first entry says more about another worker's timing than about this product. The control itself is untouched: no policy value, no configuration, no retry setting, no skip.

THE MECHANISM IN CI IS NOT ONLY PARALLELISM, which is worth recording because it changes what a reader should expect. Playwright defaults to half the cores, so a 2-core GitHub runner runs ONE worker and the suite is sequential there. The bucket is nonetheless contended, because it is a 10-second window and the spec file executed immediately after other files that sign in for real. The repair handles both causes because it observes the state rather than reasoning about who else is running.

ONE THING I FOUND BY OVER-PARALLELISING, REPORTED AS AN ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEFECT. The DEVELOPMENT suite at --workers=4 on this 2-core container fails 6 cases with 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token <, "<!DOCTYPE"' -- the Next dev server returning an error page under on-demand compilation load. At --workers=1, which is what a 2-core CI runner actually uses, the same suite is 118 passed / 24 skipped, which matches CI #180's own development notice exactly. So this is a capacity limit of `next dev` on a small machine, not a product fault, and not caused by this change: auth-rate-limit.spec.ts skips entirely in development.

CHANGES REQUESTED at 4a13f4593ee00aff71acb470d065c7cffa39b1a4, under gpt-architect's own round-110 condition, transcribed by claude-test. The reviewer wrote: "Do NOT approve PW-0602 from parser-only evidence if Windows #14 has not proven the new job", and required that for lifecycle "every observable row" be verified as PASS, FAIL, NOT-RUN with an exact reason, then classified as (A) workflow/harness defect, (B) product defect, (C) commander-only row or (D) genuinely unsupported CI row.

WHAT WINDOWS #14 (run 37172243171, head 4a13f45) PROVED, AND IT IS THE HALF THIS TASK WAS WRITTEN FOR. The e2e-desktop job CONCLUDED SUCCESS in 3m 35s. Its annotations read "openssl=C:\Program Files\OpenSSL\bin\openssl.exe; mode=development; database=none" and "expected=118 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=24 duration=134.8s". Success is the load-bearing fact: the job contains the non-vacuity guard as a FAILING step, so a run in which the desktop axis had skipped could not have concluded success. The desktop axis therefore genuinely executed on a Windows runner, on the first attempt, with retries still at zero and the same two projects CI runs. PW-0602's first REQUIRED clause is met.

WHY THIS CANNOT BE APPROVED ANYWAY. The package job CONCLUDED FAILURE with "Process completed with exit code 1", and the only other annotation is the lifecycle publisher's own notice: "NO REPORT WAS PRODUCED. The harness writes nothing when it refuses (wrong platform, missing or bad --msi), which is a fault in this workflow rather than in the product."

THAT NOTICE CANNOT SUPPORT THE CLASSIFICATION THE REVIEWER ASKED FOR, and that is the finding. The publisher runs on `!cancelled()`, so it emits that sentence whenever no report file exists -- which is equally true if the Tauri build failed, if the inventory step threw "no msi in the inventory", if the install-verifier negative check failed, or if the harness itself refused. Only two of the package job's fourteen steps carry an `id`, so nothing on the run page names the step that exited 1. A reader is therefore invited to conclude "the harness refused over a bad --msi" when the evidence does not establish it. That is the same defect this session has now corrected three times in its own instruments: a diagnostic confidently naming a cause it has not measured.

This is category A -- a workflow/harness defect -- but it is specifically a defect in the workflow's ABILITY TO BE DIAGNOSED, and it must be fixed before any row is classified, because classifying from this annotation would be guessing. Windows #13 at 4f23c1d recorded F1 PASS, F3 PASS, F4 PASS and F2 not-run, so the package job REGRESSED between 4f23c1d and 4a13f45 and the cause is not yet known.

REQUIRED BEFORE RE-REVIEW: every step in the package job carries an id; a failure-diagnostics step names the first failing step and its outcome on the run page, in the annotation channel, as ci.yml's own failure-diagnostics already does; and the "NO REPORT" message stops asserting a cause it cannot know.

The workflow is machine-checked by the method rounds 107-110 established. Every `run:` block with `shell: pwsh` is extracted from the YAML by a parser -- 8 blocks across both jobs, 1 new -- with ${{ runner.temp }} and every ${{ steps.<id>.outcome }} substituted as GitHub would substitute them, and each parse-checked with [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile under PowerShell 7.4.6: 0 files with parse errors. The YAML round-trips through a parser and reports jobs [package, e2e-desktop] with all fourteen package steps now carrying an id -- previously two did. npm run repo:validate passes.

THE NEW DIAGNOSTICS STEP WAS EXECUTED ON BOTH ITS BRANCHES rather than read. With every outcome "success" it emits the warning branch: "The job failed but no step reports a non-success outcome, so the failure is in the runner or in something this list does not name", followed by the full trail. With tauri-bundle set to failure and the two steps after it left empty, it emits "FIRST FAILING STEP: tauri-bundle (failure). Everything after it did not run." and the trail renders those two as not-reached -- which is exactly the sentence Windows #14 could not produce.

WINDOWS #14 (run 37172243171, head 4a13f4593ee00aff71acb470d065c7cffa39b1a4) IS REAL EVIDENCE AND IT SETTLES THE HALF THIS TASK WAS WRITTEN FOR.

THE e2e-desktop JOB CONCLUDED SUCCESS, 3m 35s, on the first Windows execution of a job that had never run. Its annotations, verbatim: "openssl=C:\Program Files\OpenSSL\bin\openssl.exe; mode=development; database=none (GitHub service containers are Linux-only, so the production-with-identity rung stays on Ubuntu)" and "expected=118 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=24 duration=134.8s".

WHY SUCCESS IS THE LOAD-BEARING FACT RATHER THAN THE COUNTS. The job contains "The desktop axis actually ran" as an ordinary failing step, running assert-desktop-axis-ran.mjs against the run's own JSON report. A Playwright run in which every desktop case skipped exits 0, so a job that merely invoked the suite could have been green while proving nothing -- that guard is what makes success mean the axis executed. It cannot have passed on an all-skipped report, because that is the one case it was built to refuse and was observed refusing locally. So: npm ci succeeded on windows-latest, the browser installed, the two Next servers and the loopback stub ran, openssl resolved without needing the Git fallback this workflow carries, and the desktop-target and cross-target API cases EXECUTED. 118 expected and 0 unexpected matches the Linux development run exactly, which is the right answer for the same suite in the same mode. Retries remain 0; nothing in this change touches playwright.config.ts.

PW-0602's first REQUIRED clause -- "the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu" -- is met, by a run rather than by a parser.

THE PACKAGE JOB CONCLUDED FAILURE, and this round's work is about being able to say why. Its only annotations were "Process completed with exit code 1" and the lifecycle publisher's "NO REPORT WAS PRODUCED. The harness writes nothing when it refuses (wrong platform, missing or bad --msi), which is a fault in this workflow rather than in the product."

THAT SENTENCE ASSERTS A CAUSE IT CANNOT KNOW, and that is the defect repaired here. The publisher runs on !cancelled(), so it says that whenever no report file exists -- equally true if the Tauri bundle failed, if the inventory threw "no msi in the inventory", or if the verifier negative check failed. Only two of fourteen steps had an id, so nothing on the run page named the step that exited 1. A reader was invited to conclude the harness refused over a bad --msi. Windows #13 at 4f23c1d recorded F1 PASS, F3 PASS, F4 PASS, F2 not-run, so the job REGRESSED and the cause is not yet established. Every step now has an id; a "Which step failed" step names the first non-success step with the full trail; and it additionally lists every .msi and .exe actually under the bundle directory, because "tauri-bundle=success" and "there is an installer where the inventory looks for one" are different claims. The old message no longer asserts a cause.

TWO HYPOTHESES WERE ELIMINATED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN. (1) PL-0718's tsconfig exclusion of dist was a plausible cause, since the desktop target writes its generated types there: ruled out by deleting .next, dist and next-env.d.ts and running npm run build:desktop on the resulting clean tree, which exits 0 and emits a full route table. (2) The inventory-to-lifecycle path handoff was a plausible cause, since the lifecycle step joins the bundle root with the inventory's name: ruled out by reading artifact-inventory.mjs, which records name as relative(bundleDir, path) -- "msi/<file>.msi" -- so the join is correct, and which already refuses both zero and multiple installers per kind.

WHAT IS STILL UNVERIFIED AND IS NOT CLAIMED: the cause of the package failure, and therefore the lifecycle rows for this head. No row is classified as A, B, C or D on this evidence, because classifying from an annotation that admits it does not know would be guessing. The next Windows run of this workflow names the step; that is the evidence, and this gate is not it.

message: WINDOWS #14 (run 37172243171, head 4a13f45) CONSUMED. e2e-desktop: SUCCESS, 3m35s -- 'openssl=C:\Program Files\OpenSSL\bin\openssl.exe; mode=development; database=none' and 'expected=118 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=24 duration=134.8s'. Success is load-bearing because the job carries the non-vacuity guard as a failing step, so an all-skipped desktop axis could not have been green. WHAT WAS FOUND. packages/persistence/src/migration-journal.test.ts exists because drizzle-kit does NOT read a directory of .sql files -- it reads migrations/meta/_journal.json and applies the tags listed there. The test's header records the defect it was written for: with an empty journal, the documented migrate command EXITS 0, creates zero tables, and prints "migrations applied successfully!". So a migration file that is not in the journal is a migration that silently does not exist, and the test requires the journal be non-empty and agree with the SQL on disk IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Separately, migrations/meta/0000_snapshot.json is the previous state drizzle-kit diffs against; PL-0406's own history records that without it the next generate emitted a duplicate migration re-creating all eight tables. And src/schema/index.ts holds the `schema` object the Drizzle client is constructed with and that profile-scoping.test.ts walks -- a table absent from it is a table the client cannot query and the scoping test never checks.

PATHS ADDED: packages/persistence/migrations/meta/_journal.json; packages/persistence/migrations/meta/0001_snapshot.json; packages/persistence/src/schema/index.ts.

THREE GUARDS IN THIS REPOSITORY CAUGHT THREE REAL MISTAKES WHILE THIS WAS BEING BUILT, AND NONE OF THEM WAS WEAKENED.

(1) profile-scoping.test.ts refused the table. The first version declared the primary key with a column-level .primaryKey(), which does not appear in getTableConfig(table).primaryKeys at all -- so the automatic scoping check would have passed the table WITHOUT EXAMINING IT. It is now a table-level primaryKey() with an explicit name, which also satisfies PL-0407's rule that the snapshot, the generated SQL and the database must all say the same word for a constraint.

(2) scope-forgery.test.ts refused forgetMediaPreferences. Written as store.mediaPreferences.delete(profileIdFromScope(input.scope)), the method READS AS issuance-first and is not: JavaScript evaluates the member access before the argument, so against that suite's refusing store it failed with "reached the store" instead of ForgedProfileScopeError -- it had touched storage on behalf of a capability nobody granted. The id is now derived on its own line first. "It refused" and "it refused before touching storage" are different guarantees and the suite exists to tell them apart.

(3) migration-journal.test.ts refused the ninth table, by design. Its EXPECTED_TABLES is a reviewed postcondition that exists because a defect once made db:migrate create ZERO tables while printing success. The set was updated deliberately and the describe block renamed, because leaving it reading "eight-table postcondition" while asserting nine would be a comment that lies.

THE SCOPING ASSERTION WAS ALSO SEEN TO FAIL ON PURPOSE: with the .where() removed from readMediaPreferences, repository-scoping.test.ts fails with "'readMediaPreferences' filters or writes profile_id in every statement" and passes again when restored. That suite renders the captured predicates through Drizzle's own PgDialect, so what it checks is the SQL that would be sent.

THE MIGRATION WAS APPLIED TO A REAL POSTGRESQL, not only generated. A fresh database took 0000 then 0001 cleanly and reports nine tables. \d profile_media_preference shows the columns, the text[] types, PRIMARY KEY btree (profile_id) named profile_media_preference_pkey, and the cascade. CI APPLIES MIGRATION 0000 BY NAME AND NOTHING ELSE, SO PL-0723's NEW TABLE DOES NOT EXIST IN ANY CI e2e RUN.

.github/workflows/ci.yml's 'Apply the repository migration' step is:

  psql "$LIBERTY_E2E_POSTGRES_URL" --set ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --quiet \
    --file packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql

followed by a count asserting exactly 8 tables. It does fail loudly for a migration that does not apply CLEANLY. It is silent for a migration that is never named. The same class of defect returned through the door the fix left open.

It also closes the SECOND repair this task made on itself: the round-109 changes-requested record says the diagnostics were written to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, which no fetch of two separate runs could read a single word of, and that they had to move to ::notice annotations. They did, and the annotations above are what came back.

CONDITION 2 -- CLAUSE A, PROVEN BY THE SAME FAILURE. windows-lifecycle-suite is one of the three suites this task added to the job. It ran, it failed, and it failed the build -- which is clause A's "all three execute in CI and fail the build when they fail", demonstrated rather than asserted. A suite added to CI and never seen to fail would have proven only that it was listed. The two earlier steps did not fail, so scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs -- moved after `Install dependencies` in this task's first repair -- ran in its new position without the dependency failure that exposed the mistake.

CONDITION 3 -- NO SECRET LEAKAGE. The machine annotation is an allowlist of seven named facts (cores, total memory, available memory, free disk, node, npm, NODE_OPTIONS). No environment dump, no token, no value this repository has not already published. The requirement "an allowlist of named variables, never a dump" is met on the face of the published annotation itself, which is the strongest place it could be checked.

CONDITION 4 -- NOTHING WAS WEAKENED. "DO NOT declare OOM. DO NOT increase memory merely because exit 134 occurred. DO NOT increase timeouts without evidence. DO NOT add retries to hide it." git diff 4ce4d913..4a13f45 -- .github/workflows/ci.yml contains no change to memory, NODE_OPTIONS heap sizing, timeout-minutes, retries or what the job runs, beyond ADDING the three suites clause A required. The NODE_OPTIONS the annotation reports is --report-on-fatalerror, a diagnostic flag, not a heap increase.

CONDITION 5 -- COST. Clause C asked that the job not grow materially. The three added suites are sub-second locally; the 42m 6s this run took is dominated by the control-plane suite, which was already there and which ran to completion before windows-lifecycle-suite failed.

FINGERPRINT CURRENCY, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. This approval binds to 4a13f45, the commit CI #180 actually ran. `git diff --stat 4a13f45 HEAD` over the full reviewed surface -- .github/workflows/ci.yml plus the four review dependencies package.json, scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs, apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs and scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs -- is EMPTY. The surface is byte-identical at HEAD, so the evidence and the current tree describe the same thing and no stale-approval question arises.

The failure is in scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs -- a cross-check demanding a literal that PW-0307 deliberately removed from windows.yml when it replaced an inline path assertion with a derived one -- reproduced locally as 30 tests, 29 pass, 1 fail. It is filed as PL-0727 and is not PL-0714's defect: this task's obligation was that the suite run and that a failure say something, and both are exactly what happened.

node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs: 32 tests, 7 suites, 32 pass, 0 fail, 206ms. BEFORE: 30 tests, 29 pass, 1 fail -- "agrees with the install path the Windows workflow asserts", the case CI #180's validate job went red on.

NON-VACUITY PROVEN THREE WAYS, because the case this replaces passed for a whole round while asserting something that was no longer true, and "it is green now" is exactly what it said then.

1. AGAINST THE REAL FILE, EXECUTABLE. sed -i 's/liberty-desktop.exe/liberty-player.exe/' scripts/windows/verify-install.mjs, then re-run: 32 tests, 31 pass, 1 fail -- "not ok 6 - verify-install's executable agrees with the derived executable". File restored from a copy taken first; git diff --stat on it is empty afterwards.

A third case, "A CROSS-CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL IS NOT A CROSS-CHECK", drives the same comparison function with disagreeing text and requires the refusal, and then with agreeing text and requires that it does NOT throw -- so the rule is not satisfied by a function that always throws. That one runs on every future execution; 1 and 2 were performed once, by hand, and are recorded here rather than left as a claim.

evidence:
THE STEP WAS EXTRACTED FROM THE WORKFLOW AND RUN AGAINST A REAL POSTGRESQL 16, five times, on fresh databases. Extracted with `yaml.safe_load` and taking `jobs.e2e.steps[id=migrate].run` verbatim, so what was executed is the text CI will execute, not a paraphrase of it. The workflow also parses: yaml.safe_load succeeds and reports jobs validate, e2e-typecheck, e2e.

A. CLEAN RUN, fresh database. exit 0.
   "applying 2 migration(s) in this order:
      packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql
      packages/persistence/migrations/0001_profile_media_preferences.sql
    migrations applied; all 9 declared table(s) are present"
   NINE, not eight. 0001's profile_media_preference is applied and accepted -- the two things the old step could not do. Confirmed independently: \d profile_media_preference shows the table with its primary key on profile_id.

B. LOUD FAILURE IS PRESERVED. A probe migration 0002 referencing a table that does not exist: exit 3, with
   "psql:packages/persistence/migrations/0002_broken_probe.sql:1: ERROR: relation \"absent_table\" does not exist".
   ON_ERROR_STOP and set -euo pipefail still stop the job on a migration that does not apply cleanly. Probe deleted; git status on packages/persistence is clean.

C. A NEW MIGRATION IS PICKED UP WITH NOBODY EDITING THIS STEP. A probe 0002 creating probe_table: exit 0, the order line lists three files, "all 10 declared table(s) are present", and information_schema reports probe_table present (count 1). This is the property the task asked for -- by a mechanism, not by a list somebody remembers to extend -- demonstrated rather than argued.

D. NON-VACUITY: AN EMPTY DIRECTORY MUST FAIL. Run from a scratch tree whose packages/persistence/migrations is empty: exit 1, with
   "::error::no migrations found under packages/persistence/migrations; this step would have applied nothing and passed".
   This is the exact failure shape the whole step exists to prevent -- `drizzle-kit migrate` applying nothing and exiting 0 -- and it is the one shape every other check here would have let through.

E. ORDERING IS LEXICAL AND IS PROVEN AGAINST A HOSTILE FILESYSTEM ORDER. Three probe files written in the order 0002_c, 0000_a, 0001_b, so `ls -U` (directory order) reports 0002_c, 0001_b, 0000_a. The step printed:
      0000_a.sql / 0001_b.sql / 0002_c.sql
   LC_ALL=C sort, so the runner's locale cannot change it. 0002 before 0001 would succeed on an empty database and corrupt an upgrade, which is why this is asserted rather than assumed.

F. THE POSTCONDITION NAMES ITS CASUALTY. Against a database with 0001's table dropped, the check loop produced
   "::error::the migrations declare 9 table(s); these are not in the database after applying them: profile_media_preference".
   The literal count it replaces could only ever say a number was wrong. This is strictly stronger, not weaker: it still catches a partial application, it names which table, and it grows with the migrations. The derivation itself has a non-vacuity guard -- migrations declaring no CREATE TABLE is an error, not a silently empty check.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: `drizzle-kit migrate` was not reinstated. PL-0723 generated meta/_journal.json, so it would now do something -- but "does something" is not "fails loudly", and this is not the task that can prove its behaviour. WHAT THIS TASK ADDED OR CHANGED, AND WHAT EACH ONE IS FOR:

apps/web/src/components/settings/settings.test.tsx -- 13 cases, new. The language field's PARSE is pinned over the five inputs that matter: order preserved ("ja, en, de"), whitespace and empties dropped but never a tag, an empty field answering [] rather than [""] (which would reach the endpoint and be refused for something the viewer did not type), a lossless round trip with formatLanguageList, and case left alone because the ENDPOINT owns what a language tag is and a client that lower-cased first would be a second validator whose message a viewer never sees. Two source rules on the form: it mentions no profileId anywhere (the endpoint derives the profile from the session and its contract is .strict(), so the component could not address another household's settings even by accident), and it applies state from the RESPONSE on both paths rather than from the inputs. The diagnostics section is asserted by COMPUTING decidePlaybackTelemetry independently with the same inputs and requiring the rendered page to agree, code by code -- so a change to the decision that this screen stopped reflecting fails here instead of misleading a viewer -- plus a source rule that it offers no control at all, because a toggle wired to nothing is the fake persistence the round-110 instruction forbids by name. About is asserted twice deliberately: the rendered version equals package.json's, AND the source contains no version-shaped literal, because the first assertion passes either way and only the second catches a paste.

apps/web/src/app/watch/watch-session.test.ts -- 5 cases added, 30 total, all passing. These are where the acceptance's "consumed as PW-0206's defaults" is actually proven, and they pin the three states apart: null (nobody has chosen) sends CONSERVATIVE_CAPABILITIES unchanged; a list sends it with preferredAudioLanguages replaced, IN THE VIEWER'S ORDER (asserted as a sequence, not a set -- the contract says order is meaningful); and [] sends the empty list, which is the case that forces the caller to carry `stored` rather than collapsing an opt-out into a default. A fourth pins the BLAST RADIUS -- the key set is identical to the baseline and every key except preferredAudioLanguages is unchanged, written that way so a capability field added later is covered without anybody remembering -- because every other field is a claim about what the DEVICE can decode and a settings screen must not be able to widen one. A fifth proves the list is copied, so a later mutation of the repository's array cannot change a request already described.

apps/web/src/lib/viewer-preferences.test.ts -- 3 cases, new, and the header states plainly what this environment can and cannot see. The loader resolves the REAL repository adapter and the REAL identity system, exactly as loadResumePosition does, so no store is injected and no success path is faked here. What is pinned is the property that holds in every configuration and is the one a playback page depends on: a read that cannot be satisfied answers stored:false with the neutral value rather than throwing, the direction matters (stored:true with empty lists would be an opt-out the viewer never expressed), and the shared constant it returns is frozen so one caller cannot mutate what the next render sees.

A CORRECTION MADE WHILE WRITING THIS, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS A REAL MISTAKE. The first draft of loadMediaPreferences returned MediaPreferences alone, with a comment arguing the stored/not-stored distinction "does not matter to the media engine". That was wrong, and the first caller proved it: an unconfigured profile must keep getting ["en"] and a cleared profile must get [], and both have empty lists. message:
A PLACEHOLDER SHA WAS WRITTEN INTO APPLY-ROUND-110.cmd AND IS CORRECTED, recorded because it is the one category of mistake this project refuses absolutely.

WHAT HAPPENED. Rebuilding the bundle after the handoff commit moved the target from 6697fd4 to a new head. Updating the script, I typed `set TARGET=963e6884f1a9b0ba1f2a2a3b0a0a0a0a0a0a0a0a` -- the first seven characters read off the git output and the remaining thirty-three INVENTED -- in the same breath as running `git rev-parse HEAD`, whose answer was on screen.

WHAT IT WOULD HAVE DONE. Step [7/7]'s post-check compares the landed HEAD against TARGET and refuses the tree if they differ, so Diego would have seen 'The merge reported success but HEAD is 963e6883..., not 963e6884...' and been told not to trust a tree that was in fact correct. Harmless in effect and exactly wrong in kind.

CORRECTED by passing `git rev-parse HEAD` into the edit as an argument rather than retyping it, with an assertion that the placeholder is present before and absent after. TARGET is now 963e6883c86c6942f4a9096acf6a34078117aa53. The structural checker re-run: balanced, seven of seven steps, every jump lands, fast-forward present.

WHY IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED. The standing constraint says never fabricate a value, and 'it was only a delivery script' is the sentence that makes the next one land somewhere that matters. It also happened in the same round in which I reported APPLY-ROUND-109.cmd shipping broken -- the artefact nothing in this repository checks is the one where a careless value survives, and that is an argument for checking it, which is now done.

THE READY QUEUE IS EMPTY. WHAT PREVENTS MORE WORK, DETERMINED MECHANICALLY RATHER THAN ASSERTED, AND WHY IT CANNOT BE REMOVED SAFELY.

gpt-architect's round-110 instruction: "When the READY queue empties: determine what engineering dependency is preventing more work and remove it where safely possible." This is that determination. message:
ENVIRONMENT ARTEFACT, NOT A DEFECT: ten e2e failures in this container's production+PostgreSQL run, caused by the web server dying mid-suite.

WHAT WAS SEEN. Measuring the three configurations for PL-0717, the production+PostgreSQL run reported expected=90 unexpected=10 over 151 cases. NINE of the ten are connection failures -- "apiRequestContext.post: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3177" and "page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED" -- which is not a product behaviour, it is the absence of a server. The tenth, first in order, is settings.spec.ts "a choice survives a reload" failing to find "have not chosen yet", which is what the page renders when its fetch to the API cannot be answered: the moment the server stopped responding rather than a separate fault.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE WHEN THE BOX IS NOT OVERLOADED. Re-running exactly the two affected specs (settings.spec.ts and watchlist.spec.ts) against the same production build and the same PostgreSQL: 14 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed, 32.2s. The difference is the load -- the failing run was the full --project=api --project=chromium matrix, 151 cases, on a 2-core container that was also running PostgreSQL.

WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SHRUGGED OFF. Round 110 saw the same class of thing twice (PostgreSQL dying mid-round behind three watchlist failures; next dev overwhelmed at --workers=4 producing six HTML-instead-of-JSON failures) and the standing risk is that a session learns to explain away red results. So the rule applied here is the one that was applied then: a failure is environmental only when the same thing passes on a quieter box, and that re-run is recorded beside the claim rather than asserted.

NOTHING WAS CHANGED IN RESPONSE. No timeout raised, no retry added, no worker count altered, no assertion relaxed. The container's capacity is not a property of the product.

WHAT IS STILL UNKNOWN AND IS NOT BEING GUESSED: whether CI #181's e2e job hit anything similar. CI runs on a 4-core runner with PostgreSQL as a service container, which is why the production suite has been green there, but that job has not finished and its result will be read from its own job page rather than inferred from this.

evidence:
THE THIRD CONFIGURATION RUNS, THE THREE TITLES EXECUTE IN IT, AND THE GUARD THAT SAYS SO WAS PROVEN TO REFUSE.

MEASURED FIRST, DECIDED SECOND. All three configurations were run to completion locally with a JSON reporter and their executed sets compared:

  development              ran 122  skipped 29   274.8s
  production + PostgreSQL  ran 100  skipped 51    99.0s
  production, NO database  ran  71  skipped 80    75.4s

Tests the third configuration runs that NEITHER other one does -- computed as C minus (A union B), not asserted -- are EXACTLY three:
  [api]      playback-session.api.spec.ts > a deployment with no identity system > fails closed with 503 and names the operator's remedy
  [api]      playback-session.api.spec.ts > a deployment with no identity system > publishes nothing only a resolver could know
  [chromium] watchlist.spec.ts > a deployment with no identity system refuses honestly rather than showing an empty list

Tests skipped in ALL THREE once this step exists: exactly two, both media-rig rows. They are RIG rows in PW-0601's matrix, they need the commander's hardware, and they remain skipped with their reasons intact -- which the acceptance requires and which this measurement confirms rather than hopes.

THE NARROW INVOCATION WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, WITH THE REASON. The acceptance invites naming the two spec files if that buys the same coverage for less. It was measured: the dominant cost is the production build, which either invocation pays and turbo serves from cache in this job, leaving 75 seconds of test time. Against that, naming two files would put a hand-maintained list of what matters into this workflow -- the same defect PL-0714 removed from the suite steps above it and PL-0726 removed from the migration step below it, in this very file, this round and last. A future test that became third-configuration-only would be covered by the whole-suite step and missed by the narrow one, silently, which is precisely how these three were lost for eight rounds.

THE RUN. `npm test -- --project=api --project=chromium --reporter=list,json,html` with LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=production and NO LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL. The absence is the configuration: src/env.ts derives the auth secret from that variable's presence, so a production run without it IS a deployment with no identity system. Nothing is stubbed and no test is told it is special.

`html` IS NAMED ON THE COMMAND LINE DELIBERATELY, and finding out why was a defect caught before commit: --reporter on the CLI REPLACES the config's reporter list rather than adding to it, so the first draft wrote no e2e/playwright-report at all and the upload step would have archived nothing. Verified after the fix: both /tmp/verify-reporters.json and e2e/playwright-report/index.html are produced.

THE GUARD, AND THE FIVE WAYS IT WAS PROVEN TO REFUSE. The acceptance says evidence must be "the run naming them as passed, not a count that went up", so a step reads the JSON report and requires all three BY NAME, each present and each "expected". It was extracted from the workflow with yaml.safe_load -- so what was executed is the text CI will execute -- and driven against real reports:

  A. the real third-configuration report      -> exit 0, three "ran and passed" notices naming each title and its project
  B. the real production+PostgreSQL report    -> exit 1, three errors, each saying the title is "skipped", not "expected"
  C. the real development report              -> exit 1, three errors
  D. a report with one title renamed          -> exit 1, "No test matching ... is in the report at all. It was renamed or deleted"
  E. no report file at all                    -> exit 1, "whether these three ran is unknown -- which is not the same as them having run"

B and C are the important ones: the guard is driven against the two configurations CI ACTUALLY RUNS TODAY and goes red on both. It would have caught the original defect. A sixth case arrived unplanned while verifying the reporters -- a run of only playback-session.api.spec.ts -- and it refused on the missing watchlist title.

The step also emits the suite counts as an annotation, because annotations are the only CI channel this session can read.

NOTHING WAS WEAKENED. No test was changed, no assertion relaxed, no skip removed, no retry added, no timeout raised. The two existing suite steps are untouched -- `git diff` over this file is confined to the inserted block -- so no existing configuration loses coverage.

message:
PL-0728 FILED: a standing mechanical check for "skipped in every configuration we run".

WHY, IN THE WORDS PL-0717's OWN NOTES USED. "scripts/test-validate-repo.mjs ran nowhere until PL-AI-0002; scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs and the 30-case Windows lifecycle suite ran nowhere until PL-0714; apps/web/src/components/player/tracks.ts was imported by nothing until PW-0306 wired it. Each time the thing existed, passed, and no gate asked it. A standing mechanical check for 'skipped in every configuration we run' would have found all four."

PL-0717 is the fourth instance and it was found by hand: two suite runs and a set intersection, performed by a person who happened to think of it. The same measurement, automated, is a few lines over the JSON reports the e2e job now produces for all three configurations.

WHY IT IS NOT PART OF PL-0717. PL-0717's allowedPaths is .github/workflows/ci.yml alone. The check belongs in a script file -- e2e/ or scripts/ -- and wants a place in `npm run test:scripts`, which means package.json. Widening PL-0717 to reach either would be the silent surface broadening the standing constraints forbid, and PL-0717's acceptance is specific about the three titles rather than about a general mechanism.

WHAT IT SHOULD DO, carried from the measurement that found this: read the JSON reports every configuration writes, compute the intersection of their skipped sets, and REFUSE any title in it that is not on a declared allowlist of rows that legitimately run nowhere -- today exactly the two media-rig rows, which need the commander's hardware. The allowlist is the point: a row that must stay uncovered is a decision somebody records, and a row that drifts into being uncovered is a defect.

It is filed BACKLOG rather than READY: the e2e job only began writing a JSON report for a configuration this round, and the check wants all three to do so, which is itself part of its work.
